# Audit Skill Improvements: P1–P3 Optimization Backlog

## Problem Statement

The audit skill (`skill/audit/`) has accumulated correctness gaps, performance issues, and code-quality debt from prior feature additions. This epic coordinates the systematic resolution of critical and high-priority defects followed by medium-priority refactors and polish.

## Users

- **Map (agent):** Executes `/skill:audit` on work items and expects fast, correct, reproducible audits.
- **Ralph (orchestrator):** Consumes persisted audit reports (`skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py`) to gate merge approvals.
- **Developers:** Review audit output and fix flagged issues; they rely on audit accuracy.

> **User stories (derived from children):**
> 1. As a developer, I want the audit to detect uncommitted working-tree changes so it does not produce stale verdicts.
> 2. As an operator, I want audit `wl` calls to resolve the worklog store efficiently (cached, not per-call sibling scan).
> 3. As an orchestrator, I want the audit SKILL.md to stay under ~13 KB so it fits in context windows.
> 4. As a developer, I want the audit runner to execute faster by avoiding redundant `wl show` fetches and consolidating duplicate parsers.
> 5. As a reviewer, I want the test suite to be split by concern for faster iteration and clearer failure diagnostics.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **All P1 (critical) children are closed:** `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` (done), `SA-0MSL1YX24000V2MG` (done), `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` (done).
2. **All P2 (high) children are closed:** `SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC`, `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF` (done), `SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY`.
3. **All P3 (medium) children are closed:** `SA-0MSL1Z67Z001ZO87`, `SA-0MSL1Z6M7002EDS0`, `SA-0MSL1Z70C007B9VZ`, `SA-0MSL1Z7E9005TLBA`, `SA-0MSL1ZB5J005ENLI`, `SA-0MSL1ZBJO00411KU`, `SA-0MSL1ZBY0007PIVD`.
4. **Full project test suite passes** (`/skill:test`) with no new failures.
5. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.

## Constraints

- **No behavioral regression** in the audit verdict (accept/no-accept/timeout) logic — all changes must be verified against existing test coverage.
- **Children must be worked sequentially by priority:** P1 first (critical defects → correctness), then P2 (high → correctness/performance), then P3 (medium → quality/efficiency).
- **All changes in worktrees** per the implement skill — never edit the main checkout directly.
- **SKILL.md must remain under ~13 KB** after restructure (child `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF` already achieved this).

## Existing State

| Area | Current state |
|---|---|
| **SKILL.md** | 12.8 KB (restructured from 44 KB by `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF`) |
| **audit_runner.py** | ~1200-line `cmd_issue()`, 251 tests in monolithic `test_audit_runner.py`, uses `git HEAD sha` + description hash for fingerprint (misses working-tree state) |
| **Worklog-dir resolution** | Cached by `SA-0MSL1YX24000V2MG` |
| **Dead code** | Removed in `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` |
| **Duplicate parsers** | Consolidated by `SA-0MSL1Z15600760KC` |
| **Pre-flight affirmation** | Documented in SKILL.md, implemented/removed by `SA-0MSL1Z1WU005O5IY` |
| **Duplicated helpers** | `_record_script_failure` closures, `SCANNING` block constant, ISO-8601 freshness timestamp parsing |
| **Redundant fetches** | Multiple `wl show` calls per audit run |
| **Doc drift** | `./scripts/failure_notice.py` path in SKILL.md does not resolve |

## Desired Change

All 13 children (P1→P2→P3) implemented, each delivering its own measurable improvement, resulting in a faster, more correct, and maintainable audit skill.

## Risks & Assumptions

| Risk | Likelihood | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|
| **P1 bug fix (`SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ`) introduces regressions** | Medium | Preserve existing fingerprint output for git-HEAD-only runs; add regression test covering HEAD-only scenario |
| **`cmd_issue` decomposition (~1200 lines) breaks existing behavior** | High | Extract with zero behavior change; verify via full test suite; commit incrementally |
| **Test split (`SA-0MSL1ZBJO00411KU`) increases maintenance burden** | Low | Split by concern only; maintain one test per logical audit step |
| **P3 children conflict with each other** | Low | Children are independently scoped; verify before implementing |
| **Scope creep — adding improvements beyond the 13 children** | Medium | Record opportunities as new work items; do not add to this epic's scope |

**Assumptions:**
- Each child's acceptance criteria are accurate and testable (verified at child intake)
- The `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` contract does not change during this epic
- All children are independently implementable (no inter-child dependencies beyond priority ordering)

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Operational brief (already restructured to ~12.8 KB)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Core runner (~1200 lines, `cmd_issue()` target for decomposition)
- `skill/audit/scripts/scan.py` — Grep-based scanning
- `skill/audit/scripts/persist_audit.py` — Audit report persistence
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner.py` — 251-test monolith to be split by concern
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — Shared status lifecycle context manager
- `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py` — Pi JSON-stream parser (duplicate + latent bug)
- `skill/scripts/failure_notice.py` — Failure notice template (doc drift fix)
- `skill/audit/tests/` — Test directory to grow with split tests

## Related Work

| Work Item | Title | Stage |
|---|---|---|
| `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` | Working-tree state in content fingerprint (stale-audit gap) | done |
| `SA-0MSL1YX24000V2MG` | Cache worklog-dir resolution | done |
| `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` | Remove/wire discarded Pi model call in cmd_project | done |
| `SA-0MSL1Z1J50038RBF` | Restructure SKILL.md into operational brief + deep docs | done |
| `SA-0MSG48MEI0083K82` | CRITICAL: Audit runner cwd-independence broken | — |
| `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` | Audit runner has circular dependency (child blocks parent) | — |
| `SA-0MS3G0D6A009TM81` | Phase 2 code review doesn't always happen | — |

---

## Plan: Changelog

| Time (UTC) | Action |
|---|---|
| 2026-08-13T04:29Z | Plan skill run: 6 automated review stages passed. Recommended execution order updated (test split before decomposition; doc drift fix early). 3 open questions recorded in comments. |

---

## Appendix: Clarifying Questions

No interview questions were asked — the seed context (epic description + 13 children with individual ACs) was sufficient. The plan skill ran 6 automated review stages with findings documented.

**Open Questions (from effort/risk assessment):**

1. Q: Scope of Pre-flight affirmation — implement fully or remove?
   Answer (plan): Recommend implementing lightweight guard (status check + `--force` bypass) rather than full removal, since the documentation exists and a cheap guard adds value.

2. Q: cmd_issue decomposition — how many phases is optimal?
   Answer (plan): 5-6 named phases as suggested in the child AC, operating on a small context dataclass.

3. Q: Test split strategy — by concern, by test type, or by feature?
   Answer (plan): By concern (matches existing split pattern in the audit test directory).

## Summary

The project-level audit path (`cmd_project` in `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 5163) invokes `_call_pi_and_maybe_log("project", "project", ...)` but discards the result entirely:

```python
pi_result = _call_pi_and_maybe_log("project", "project", prompt, ...)
if pi_result.get("verdict") == "met" and pi_result.get("evidence"):
    pass  # Could enhance this in future
```

The model output never affects `summary`, `recommendation`, or the assembled report. Every project audit wastes model tokens, up to 1800s wall-clock, and an audit concurrency slot with zero effect on the output.

## Expected behaviour

Either wire the Pi output into the project report (parse `summary`/`recommendation` from the model JSON, using the locally-computed values as fallback), or remove the call and the unused prompt entirely. No model call whose output is discarded may remain.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No Pi model call is made whose output is discarded — the project report either uses the model output (with local fallback) or makes no model call.
2. Existing project-audit output format (`wl list`-derived summary/recommendation) is preserved when the model path is unavailable/fails.
3. Unit tests cover both the wired path and the fallback path (including Pi failure).
4. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` passes green.

## Summary

`_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix` in `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` (line ~183) re-runs `glob("*/.worklog/config.yaml")` and re-reads every sibling project's config on **every** call. The audit runner's `_run_wl` invokes this resolution per `wl` command (via `resolve_worklog_flags`). A multi-child item audit makes dozens of `wl` calls; when the runner is launched from the skill install directory (a documented, supported usage), every call pays the full sibling scan.

## Expected behaviour

Add `functools.lru_cache` (or equivalent memoization) to `_find_worklog_dir_by_prefix`. The prefix→dir mapping cannot change mid-process, so caching is safe. This is shared code — verify no other caller (e.g. `status_lifecycle` itself, other skills) depends on re-scanning behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

1. The sibling scan runs at most once per process per prefix (observable via test instrumentation).
2. Resolution results are byte-identical to the current behavior for hit and miss cases.
3. Existing `test_status_lifecycle.py` and audit worklog-dir tests pass.
4. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/ skill/shared/tests/` passes green.
data.title: Cache worklog-dir resolution to stop per-wl-call sibling scans

## Summary

**Bug (stale-audit correctness gap).** `_compute_content_fingerprint` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, ~line 696) fingerprints only: git HEAD sha + work-item description hash + Key Files list. However, the audit's own file-scope manifest reads `git status --porcelain` (untracked/modified files) and the deep-analysis model reads the **working tree**, not just HEAD. So uncommitted code changes between audits do **not** invalidate freshness — the freshness gate can serve a stale audit for code that has since changed.

The docs claim "a change in ANY fingerprint component invalidates freshness", but working-tree state is not a component.

## Expected behaviour

Include the working-tree state in the fingerprint payload: a hash of `git status --porcelain` + `git diff --name-only HEAD` output (sorted, deterministic). A change in any uncommitted file, untracked file, or commit invalidates freshness; an untouched repo keeps the same fingerprint.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Modifying an uncommitted tracked file invalidates the fingerprint (stale audit → re-run).
2. Adding an untracked file invalidates the fingerprint.
3. Committing a change also invalidates (via the existing HEAD sha component).
4. An untouched working tree + unchanged description + unchanged Key Files keeps the same fingerprint (freshness preserved).
5. Unit tests cover all four cases; `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` passes green.
data.title: Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (stale-audit gap)

## Summary

`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` (~lines 1442–1560) duplicates ~120 lines of `extract_pi_text`, `parse_pi_json_line`, `_extract_text_from_content`, `_extract_text_from_assistant_message`, and `_extract_last_assistant_message_text` that already exist in `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py`.

**Latent bug in the shared copy:** the runner's local `_parse_pi_json_line` has a fix the shared `pi_utils.py` version lacks — it skips `message_start` events whose `role` is `user` (the prompt echo), which previously caused false parse failures. `skill/audit/audit_pr.py` imports the **shared** unguarded copy, so it can hit that false-parse bug.

## Expected behaviour

Consolidate the parsers into `skill/scripts/pi_utils.py`, adding the `role != "assistant"` guard to the shared `parse_pi_json_line`. Have `audit_runner.py` and `audit_pr.py` import from the shared module. No behavioral change to audit verdicts.

## Acceptance criteria

1. `audit_runner.py` no longer defines its own Pi JSON-stream parsers (imports from `pi_utils`).
2. `pi_utils.parse_pi_json_line` skips user-role `message_start` events (guard present) — covered by a regression test that would fail on the unguarded version.
3. `audit_pr.py` covered by a regression test for the prompt-echo false-parse case.
4. All 344+ audit tests and pi_utils tests pass; `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.

## Summary

`skill/audit/SKILL.md` lines 22–24 document a "Pre-flight affirmation": "Verify absence before proceeding to the audit flow. Confirm that the work item is ready for audit and that no active conflicting processes exist." **No code implements this.**

The concurrency semaphore (`skill/shared/process_semaphore.py`) caps concurrent pi subprocesses host-wide, but does not prevent two audits of the **same** work item racing: both set `in_progress`, both run the pipeline, and the last writer wins on persist + status transition.

## Expected behaviour

Decide and implement one of:
- **Implement:** a cheap guard in `cmd_issue` — if the item's status is already `in_progress` at entry (i.e. someone/something else is mid-audit) and `--force` is not given, warn and abort (or wait) instead of racing.
- **Remove:** rewrite the SKILL.md section to describe the actual behavior (status lifecycle + concurrency cap only).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Docs and code no longer diverge: either the guard is implemented and tested, or the SKILL.md section is corrected.
2. If implemented: an `in_progress` item without `--force` does not start a competing audit; `--force` bypasses the guard; the status lifecycle otherwise unchanged.
3. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.
data.title: Implement or remove the unimplemented Pre-flight affirmation

## Summary

`cmd_issue` performs several redundant `wl show` fetches of the same work item:
1. `wl show` (capture original status/stage)
2. `wl show --children` (main pipeline)
3. `_check_audit_freshness` may issue another `wl show` (time-gate path)
4. Per child: `_get_child_audit_verdict` issues `wl show` for freshness; the auto-trigger loop may call `_check_audit_freshness` again for the same child

Each is a subprocess spawn plus (without the worklog-dir cache, see the cache work item) a sibling-dir scan.

## Expected behaviour

Pass already-fetched work-item data through callers where the data is available (e.g. `_check_audit_freshness` accepts a `work_item` argument like `_compute_content_fingerprint` already does). Do not change wl command semantics or freshness behavior.

## Acceptance criteria

1. No duplicate `wl show` of the same item where the data is already in hand; measured per-run `wl` subprocess count for a single-child audit drops (test instrumented via the injectable runner).
2. Freshness and status-capture behavior unchanged.
3. `python3 -m pytest skill/audit/tests/` green.

Never fabricate or override a verdict.

## Context

Parent SA-0MSL51XSF0086KM5 (AC3 + AC4). A runaway audit must be stopped cleanly and the work item left in a recoverable state. The mitigation must mirror the runner's own failure-fallback semantics (restore pre-audit status/stage, clear assignee — SA-0MQJONW3C007SZQY) without ever persisting a fabricated report or overriding a completed runner verdict. Guidance-only: no script changes.

## Files to modify

- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (add the Abort & Mitigate subsection under `Monitored Run Execution`)

## Acceptance Criteria

1. SKILL.md defines the going-astray triggers: (a) stall — no new log output for >=10 minutes; (b) repeated failures — >=3 consecutive `Warning: Pi call failed` / provider-error retries with no progress; (c) other agent-determined signals (unexpected exit, error loops, output violating the audit contract) and budget exhaustion at 180 min
2. SKILL.md defines the abort procedure: kill the process tree, then apply the runner's failure-fallback semantics — restore the pre-audit `status`/`stage` captured before launch and clear the assignee (only when the runner did not already complete its verdict-driven lifecycle)
3. SKILL.md requires appending a failure notice with a progress summary (elapsed time, last phase marker, trigger) to the run log
4. SKILL.md requires reporting the outcome to the operator and explicitly forbids persisting a fabricated audit report on abort and forbids overriding a completed runner verdict (a transient abort must never demote an `in_review` item to `open`)

- Add the Abort & Mitigate subsection to SKILL.md with the trigger thresholds, the kill/restore/clear sequence (copy-paste-ready commands), and the failure-notice + operator-report steps

# Intake brief — audit_runner: git file-scope/HEAD resolution is cwd-dependent despite cwd-independence claims

**Work item:** SA-0MSLLGDW00098UCC · `bug` · `high`

> **Headline:** The audit runner's git-based pieces (project root, file-scope manifest, changed-file list, HEAD sha, working-tree hash) resolve against the launch cwd instead of the audited project, so audits run with `--worklog-dir` from a non-project cwd verify against the wrong repository and emit invalid verdicts. Fix: resolve git against the worklog-derived owning project root, abort on undeterminable ownership, and correct the docs' scope claims.

## Problem statement

The audit runner claims cwd independence ("the runner can be launched from the skill install directory (or any other cwd) and still audit items in a different project's worklog"), but every git-based piece — project root, file-scope manifest, changed-file list, HEAD sha, working-tree hash — resolves against the **launch cwd's** repository. Launching with `--worklog-dir <project>/.worklog` from a non-project cwd therefore produces file-scope manifests, changed-file lists, and HEAD attestations from the wrong repo (observed twice on WL-0MSKSZBEL0025CN3: ContextHub audited against SorraAgents), yielding invalid audit verdicts.

## Users

- Developers/agents running `audit_runner.py issue <id> --worklog-dir <owning>/.worklog` from a non-project cwd (the documented cwd-independent pattern) — currently get wrong-scope git data (file-scope manifest, changed-file list, content-fingerprint HEAD sha, `--green-run HEAD` attestation).
- Operators relying on the launch-context guard's fail-fast guarantee.

### Example user stories

- As an agent auditing a work item from the skill install directory with `--worklog-dir <owning>/.worklog`, I want the file-scope manifest, changed-file list, and HEAD attestation to reflect the audited project, so my verdicts are valid.
- As an operator, I want an undeterminable project scope to abort loudly rather than silently audit the wrong repository.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Git pieces target the owning project.** When the runner resolves an owning project root from the worklog (explicit `--worklog-dir` parent → prefix-to-sibling scan), `_git_changed_files`, `_repo_index`, `_resolve_audited_head`, and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` resolve git against that root — **not** the launch cwd. Verified by a test simulating a launch from an unrelated cwd (e.g. skill install dir) with `--worklog-dir` pointing at the audited project: the file-scope manifest and HEAD sha must match the audited project's tree.
2. **Undeterminable ownership aborts.** When the owning project root cannot be determined (no `--worklog-dir`, unknown item prefix, no sibling match), the runner aborts with a clear error before any phase runs — it must not fall back to the launch cwd's repo for git-derived content.
3. **No regression for owning-project launches.** Launching from inside the owning project (standard path) and from a worktree of the owning project (same git repository) continues to work; a worktree launch still resolves git to the worktree checkout (never the `--worklog-dir` parent's main checkout), so worktree-only changes and the worktree branch HEAD stay correct.
4. **All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries** — `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` must state the corrected scope semantics precisely (git-derived content follows the worklog; remaining `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` consumers are still launch-cwd-bound).
5. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (existing `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner*.py` suites + new coverage; no CI/CD pipeline tests).

## Constraints

- **Scope limited to git-based resolution.** Making `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` itself per-audit dynamic (code-quality scan project_root, debug-log path, `_repo_index` fallback listing) is out of scope — tracked as follow-up work item `Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic (full cwd independence) (SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15)`.
- **Worktree correctness:** the fix must reuse the guard's existing same-repository detection (`_same_git_repository`, `audit_runner.py:770`) so a launch from `<owning>/.worklog/worktrees/<id>-<slug>` keeps resolving git to the worktree checkout, not the `--worklog-dir` parent.
- **Behavior parity:** launching from inside the owning project must behave exactly as today.
- Git remains best-effort for the freshness gate and `--green-run` fallback (missing HEAD ⇒ no attestation, partial ACs) — only *scope* undeterminability is fatal (AC2).

## Existing state

- `_detect_project_root()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:681`) resolves `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` **at import time** from the launch cwd's `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` (fallback `Path.cwd()`).
- `_default_runner` (`:592`) runs `subprocess.run` with **no cwd**, so `_git_changed_files` (`:2953`), `_repo_index` (`:2983`), `_resolve_audited_head` (`:1348`), and `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (`:1080`) all resolve git against the launch cwd.
- `_resolve_owning_project_root` (`:792`) already resolves the owning project from `--worklog-dir` (parent) → prefix scan; `_verify_launch_context` (`:806`) uses it for the fail-fast launch-context guard (LP-0MSQ32HNR007AI6B), including same-repo/worktree handling (`:813–818`).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` (lines ~155–193) and `skill/audit/SKILL.md` (~line 55) document that `wl` resolution is cwd-independent but *project scope is launch-cwd-only* ("`--worklog-dir` does not change the project scope; only the launch directory does") — this claim is what the repro contradicts for the git-based pieces.

## Desired change

- Resolve a per-audit **git target root** from the worklog (explicit `--worklog-dir` parent → prefix-to-sibling scan), reusing `_resolve_owning_project_root`; run the git-based pieces (`_git_changed_files`, `_repo_index`, `_resolve_audited_head`, `_resolve_working_tree_hash`, and the file-scope/content-fingerprint callers) against it (e.g. `git -C <root>` or a runner with an explicit cwd).
- When the owning root cannot be determined, abort with a clear error (AC2) instead of resolving against the launch cwd.
- Keep worktree same-repo semantics so worktree launches resolve to the worktree checkout (AC3).
- Update `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` to state the corrected scope semantics (AC4).

**Key Files:**

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_git_changed_files` (:2953), `_repo_index` (:2983), `_resolve_audited_head` (:1348), `_resolve_working_tree_hash` (:1080) to target the worklog-derived owning root; `_resolve_owning_project_root` (:792) reused as the resolution basis; `_default_runner` (:592) / new cwd-aware runner; content-fingerprint + file-scope callers (`_compute_content_fingerprint` :1034, `_build_file_scope_manifest` :3040).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — correct the cwd-independence / scope claim (~line 55).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — correct the cwd-independence section (lines ~155–193).
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_launch_context.py` — extend with non-owning-cwd + `--worklog-dir` git-resolution tests; worktree-launch regression test.
- `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_worklog_dir.py` — extend if it covers git resolution paths.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSAXHBS5008R97M` — Tests: cwd-independent wl lifecycle and diagnostics (completed; the wl side of cwd independence).
- `SA-0MSG48MEI0083K82` — [CRITICAL] Audit runner cwd-independence broken: worklog store not resolved when launched outside the audited project (completed; the earlier wl-resolution bug this item mirrors on the git side).
- `SA-0MSL1YXG7004F2BZ` — Include working-tree state in the audit content fingerprint (completed; consumes `git status --porcelain`, cwd-dependent today).
- `SA-0MSKB6US1009CNHT` — Audit: content-based freshness gate (completed; consumes HEAD sha + Key Files fingerprint).
- `SA-0MSGLAVCZ002LVZ4` — Audit runner: verify execution-dependent ACs via operator-attested green test run (completed; `--green-run HEAD` attestation path).
- `SA-0MS1XC2MW003XHD8` — Code quality scan uses hardcoded REPO_ROOT from script location instead of project CWD (completed; same class of bug, fixed for the code-quality scan).
- `SA-0MSKM2LSP006L0K8` — audit_runner crashes when Phase 2 evidence is a dict (open; same file, unrelated defect).
- Docs: `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md`, `skill/audit/SKILL.md`.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Scope semantics — should `--worklog-dir`/prefix scan now fully determine the project scope (option a), or should the launch-context guard remain authoritative for scope with only the git internals following the owning root (option b)?" — Answer (operator, interactive): "Explain more about the question and the impact of each answer" → explained (see turn 2); working assumption **(b)** pending final confirmation in draft review. Impact summary: (a) full cwd independence but large blast radius (per-audit `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT`, guard inversion, worktree-detection requirement, conflicts with "limited to git"); (b) surgical, fixes the named failure mode at the source, reuses existing guard/worktree logic, but requires docs correction and leaves full cwd independence to a follow-up item.
- Q2: "Fallback when ownership is undeterminable — (a) fall back to launch-cwd behavior (status quo, fail-open), or (b) abort with an error?" — Answer (operator, interactive): **b** (abort). Source: interactive reply (this session). Research: `_verify_launch_context` fail-opens today (returns None when ownership is undeterminable) — AC2 turns the git layer into the abort point; no existing precedent for aborting on unknown prefix, so this is net-new guard behavior scoped to the git resolution.
- Q3: "`TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` breadth — make it per-audit dynamic, or limit the fix to the git file-scope/HEAD pieces?" — Answer (operator, interactive): **limited to git; create a work item for related broader work**. Source: interactive reply. → follow-up work item created: `Audit runner: make TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT per-audit dynamic (full cwd independence) (SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15)`, discovered-from this item.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope-creep risk:** full per-audit `TARGET_PROJECT_ROOT` (code-quality scan, debug-log path, repo-index fallback) and guard-policy change are explicitly out of scope — recorded as follow-up work item SA-0MSRLECW2001AA15, not scope.
- **Worktree regression risk:** if the fix blindly points git at the `--worklog-dir` parent, worktree audits would attest the main checkout's HEAD and miss worktree-only changes — mitigated by AC3 (reuse `_same_git_repository`/worktrees logic).
- **Assumption:** the launch-context guard stays authoritative for the non-git scope consumers (per working assumption b) — if the operator picks (a), the guard, its tests, and the docs change in this item instead of the follow-up.
- **Assumption:** git is available in audit environments (all git pieces already fail open/graceful today; only scope undeterminability becomes fatal, per AC2).

## Related work (automated report — find_related)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MLQ8ZKKM1AVGPJQ** – finish-work Subcommand (completed)
- **SA-0MM01V1HM0JA8XVL** – Enable Discord bot interactive buttons (MVP) (completed)
- **SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS** – Reduce initial LLM context from skills and skill-related startup files (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/worktrees/wl-SA-0MSQ8MXXI0029B5M-fix-child-verdict-test-contract/skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acs, agent, also, attestation, attested (+90 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acs, agent, also, ancestor, attestation (+90 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: acs, agent, also, attestation, attested (+90 more)

# Intake Brief: Plan/intake skills iterate over children & verify AC coverage

## Problem statement

When the `plan` or `intake` skills run on a work item that has child work items,
they currently process only the target item — they never descend into the
children. This leaves parent/child AC coverage unverified: a parent's acceptance
criteria may not be collectively covered by its children's ACs, and children are
never themselves planned/intaked (so the decomposition tree can be incomplete
or inconsistent at depth).

## Users

- **Agents running `/skill:plan`** on an epic or other parent with children —
  need the skill to recurse over the whole tree so every level is planned, and
  to verify that the union of child ACs covers the parent ACs.
- **Agents running `/skill:intake`** on a parent with children — need intake to
  run per child (when children exist) and to verify cross-level AC coverage.
- **Operators** — get decomposition trees whose ACs are guaranteed (or
  explicitly flagged) to cover their parents, with gaps auto-closed where
  resolvable and hard conflicts surfaced instead of silently passing.

Example user stories:

- As an agent planning an epic with children, I want the plan skill to iterate
  the whole subtree (respecting dependency order) so I don't have to invoke
  `/skill:plan` per child manually.
- As an agent planning a parent, I want a final review step that verifies the
  children's ACs collectively cover the parent's ACs, auto-closing gaps it can
  resolve and stopping with a clear report when it cannot, so a `plan_complete`
  stage is only reached when coverage is guaranteed.
- As an operator re-running intake on a decomposed epic, I want intake to verify
  AC coverage across the existing children (and per child when configured) so
  the tree stays coherent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **AC1 (tree iteration — plan):** Running `/skill:plan` on a work item with
  children processes the entire subtree, not just the target: the skill
  iterates children (each child's own plan run, recursing to any depth), in
  dependency order first (`wl dep` edges), then listed order. Verified by a
  test with a multi-level tree (parent → children → grandchildren) asserting
  every node is planned and the processing order respects `wl dep` edges.
- **AC2 (tree iteration — intake):** Running `/skill:intake` on a work item
  with children runs intake per child (recursing the subtree) and also verifies
  AC coverage across existing children. Verified by a test where intake on a
  parent with children runs per child and reports coverage.
- **AC3 (collective coverage):** After processing, for every parent node in the
  tree, the union of its children's acceptance criteria collectively covers the
  parent's acceptance criteria (each parent AC is covered by at least one child
  AC). Verified by a coverage-check test with a parent whose ACs are covered
  by children and a negative test where coverage is missing.
- **AC4 (final review step — auto-close & stop):** The skills' final review
  step closes coverage gaps it can resolve unambiguously (e.g. adding a missing
  child AC that directly maps to an uncovered parent AC), and when a gap or
  conflict cannot be resolved, stops and reports rather than advancing
  (`plan_complete`/`intake_complete` not set; item left `open` with a comment
  describing the conflict). Verified by tests: one where an unambiguous gap is
  auto-closed, one where an unresolvable conflict prevents stage advancement.
- **AC5 (docs & tests):** All related documentation is updated to reflect the
  changes (plan SKILL.md, intake SKILL.md, shared helper docstrings), and the
  full project test suite passes with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Worklog API only:** read children via `wl show <id> --children --json`;
  dependency edges via `wl dep list <id> --json`. No direct worklog file edits.
- **No work item for the process itself:** the skills must not create a work
  item to track the iteration itself.
- **Idempotence:** re-running must not create duplicate children or duplicate
  comments; existing children are reused/updated per the existing plan-skill
  idempotence rules.
- **Status lifecycle:** all status transitions go through `StatusLifecycle`
  (intake via `intake.py`, plan via `StatusLifecycle.update_status`); the new
  final review step must leave the item in a valid terminal status (`open`,
  `blocked`, or `completed`) even when it stops on an unresolvable conflict.
- **Conservative auto-closing:** only close gaps that are unambiguous (a child
  AC that clearly maps to an uncovered parent AC). Never invent requirements —
  if intent is unclear, record an Open Question / stop instead.
- **Scope:** affects the `plan` and `intake` skills (SKILL.md workflows) and
  their shared helpers. Must not change audit, implement, or other skills'
  behavior. Must not alter the audit skill's parent-child verdict semantics.

## Existing state

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` decomposes the target into child feature work items;
  it creates children (Process step 7) and runs six automated review stages on
  the freshly generated feature plan, but never recurses into children and has
  no AC-coverage check across the tree. Its "Automated review on existing
  content" path (skip decision) reviews existing content but still does not
  iterate the tree.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` prepares a single work item (claim → gather → draft →
  five mini-reviews → find-related → finish). It has no child iteration or
  coverage verification.
- `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` provides shared autoplan/approval-gate logic;
  it has no tree/coverage helpers.
- `wl` supports `wl show <id> --children --json` and `wl dep list/add/rm`, so
  tree traversal and ordering data are available without new CLI work.
- The audit skill already has parent/child awareness (child stage checks,
  inherited passes) — a useful reference for tree semantics but NOT to be
  modified by this item.

## Desired change

- **Shared helper (new or extended):** a module (e.g.
  `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` or new functions in `plan_helpers.py`) that:
  1. Fetches the full descendant tree via `wl show <id> --children --json`.
  2. Orders siblings by `wl dep` edges (topological) then listed order.
  3. Extracts ACs from each item's description (`## Acceptance Criteria`
     section).
  4. Computes coverage: for each parent AC, whether any child AC covers it.
  5. Auto-closes unambiguous gaps; returns an explicit list of unresolvable
     conflicts.
- **Plan skill:** add a "tree iteration" step (before/around Process step 7)
  that recurses into children; add a final "AC coverage review" step after the
  six review stages that applies the helper, auto-closes gaps, and on
  unresolvable conflicts stops without advancing the stage (leaving the item
  `open` with a conflict comment).
- **Intake skill:** add a per-child intake pass (when children exist) and a
  final AC-coverage verification step mirroring the plan behavior.
- **Tests:** unit tests for the shared helper (tree fetch/order, AC extraction,
  coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection) plus skill-workflow
  tests asserting stage advancement is blocked on unresolvable conflicts.

## Key Files

- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — Add tree-iteration and final AC-coverage review steps
  to the Process section.
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add per-child intake pass and AC-coverage
  verification step.
- `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py` (new) — Shared tree traversal, ordering,
  AC extraction, coverage computation, gap auto-close, conflict detection
  (or equivalent functions added to `skill/plan/plan_helpers.py` if shared
  placement is not preferred).
- `skill/plan/tests/test_plan_helpers.py` — Extend with tree/coverage helper
  tests (or add `skill/shared/tests/test_tree_coverage.py`).
- `skill/intake/tests/` — Workflow tests for per-child intake and coverage
  stop/advance behavior.

## Related work

- `SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E` — Audit runner circular dependency fix; documents the
  audit skill's child-stage semantics (children in `in_review` don't block
  parent closure). Reference only; not to be modified here.
- `SA-0MSK9IOEF007PP5S` — Audit skill: reduce wall-clock time; example of a
  parent item decomposed into children via the plan skill.
- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` — Reduce initial LLM context; an epic with 6 children,
  useful as a real-world tree for manual validation of the new iteration.
- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — Already has child-aware logic (recursive child
  implementations, terminal-stage checks); a pattern reference for how skills
  handle trees.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` + `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — Parent/child
  verdict and stage semantics; reference for tree behavior conventions.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk: recursion depth/time.** Deep trees could make plan/intake slow or
  loop. Mitigation: recursion bounded by the actual tree; each child processed
  once; idempotent re-runs. Note: no explicit depth cap is assumed unless
  needed — flag in implementation if cycles are possible in worklog trees.
- **Risk: AC extraction brittleness.** Descriptions vary in formatting; ACs may
  be missing or malformed. Mitigation: tolerant extraction; missing ACs treated
  as an uncovered gap reported to the user rather than silently ignored.
- **Risk: auto-closing gaps could invent content.** Mitigation: only
  unambiguous, directly-mapped gaps are auto-closed; everything else stops with
  a report (per AC4).
- **Assumption:** worklog trees are acyclic (a work item's children cannot
  contain it). If a cycle is ever detected, the skill stops and reports.
- **Assumption:** `wl dep list <id> --json` output shape is stable; the helper
  parses both object and array JSON shapes (per existing plan skill guidance).
- **Scope-creep note:** any additional "verify child ACs against parent at
  audit time" ideas are out of scope for this item (audit behavior unchanged)
  and would be tracked as separate work items.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q1: "Should the iteration recurse through the entire tree (a parent with

# Intake Brief — Eliminate wasteful `wl list` usage across skills

## Problem statement

AGENTS.md now prohibits unfiltered `wl list` (bare `wl list --json` or filter-only variants dump the entire worklog — up to **5.3 MB / 1861 full records** — and the whole dump is re-transmitted on every subsequent agent request). Despite this, 12 skill files still invoke `wl list`, several of them dumping 353 KB–5.3 MB of irrelevant data per call. The most wasteful call (`wl list --status completed`) returns 4.9 MB of which **1638 of 1643 items are `stage=done` (already released)** and are immediately filtered out by the calling script's own logic.

## Users

- **Agents running `/skill:audit`, `/skill:plan`, the ship release pipeline, triage, and code-review.** Every run currently pays the full-worklog token tax.
- **Operators running releases.** The ship gates (audit, critical-items, changelog) each re-dump the same 4.9 MB completed-item set.

### User stories

- As an agent running `/skill:audit`, I want a project-level status that fits in a few KB so I don't burn ~1.3M tokens on a full worklog dump.
- As a release operator, I want the release gates to query only the items they actually check so the release script doesn't process 4.9 MB of already-released items.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Every `wl list` invocation across `~/.pi/agent/skills/` follows AGENTS.md: it must include a search term, a scoping filter (`--parent`, `--status`, `--stage`, `--priority`, `--tags`), or be replaced by a scoped command (`wl show --children`, `wl next`, `wl in_progress`, `wl recent`, `wl search`).
2. The two agent-facing instructions (audit/SKILL.md, plan/SKILL.md) no longer instruct agents to run bare `wl list --json`; the dead `wl blocked` command is removed from audit/SKILL.md.
3. The ship release gates (check-audit-gate.js, check-critical-items.js, generate-changelog.js) no longer call `wl list --status completed`; payload per gate drops from ~4.9 MB to ≤ ~40 KB, verified by measuring before/after output sizes.
4. All script behavior is unchanged: unit tests for the touched scripts pass, and a dry-run of each script produces the same logical result set (verified via existing test suites in `skill/*/tests/` and `tests/`).
5. The duplicate `code-review` vs `code_review` packages are either both fixed or consolidated (flagged to operator for decision).
6. All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

> **Note:** CHANGELOG.md is **excluded** from this list. It is managed automatically by the ship skill's release pipeline. Implementing agents should not manually update CHANGELOG.md.

## Constraints

- Scripts that need full item fields (description, issueType, needsProducerReview, createdAt) **cannot** switch to `wl search`, which returns compact snippets only (id/title/status/priority + snippet).
- FTS does **not** index comments (verified: a string present in 2,254 comments returns 0 `wl search` hits) — comment-scanning cannot be replaced by `wl search`.
- Do not change worklog semantics or the wl CLI itself; this is a query-usage optimization only.
- Follow AGENTS.md query discipline: `wl list <term>` (LIKE match, full records) or `wl search <term>` (compact snippets), combined with scoping filters; never filter-only dumps.

## Existing state

- Full `wl list --json` = **5.3 MB** (1,861 items).
- `wl list --status completed --json` = **4.9 MB** (1,643 items: 1,638 `done` + 5 `in_review`).
- `wl list --status open --json` = 353 KB; `wl list --status in-progress --json` = 43 KB.
- `wl list --priority critical --json` = 94 KB; critical+open = 12 KB; critical+in-progress = 3.8 KB.
- `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --json` = 52 KB; with `--status open` added = 55 bytes (0 candidates today).
- `wl list --parent <id>` for the largest parent (342 children) = 383 KB; with `--number 1` = 1.1 KB.
- `wl search <term> --json` = compact snippets (9.4 KB for 10 critical results).
- `wl next` = 12 KB; `wl in_progress` = 39 KB; `wl recent --number 5` = 25 KB.

## Desired change

Replace every wasteful `wl list` with the smallest query that satisfies the caller's intent:

### 1. audit/SKILL.md line 19 (agent-facing; 5.3 MB dump)

**Intent:** project-level status overview when no work-item ID is present.
**Current:** `wl list --json`, `wl in_progress --json`, `wl blocked --json` (note: `wl blocked` is a **dead command** — `error: unknown command 'blocked'`).
**Alternative:** drop the full dump; use scoped commands only:
- `wl next --json` — next recommended item (12 KB)
- `wl in_progress --json` — active work (39 KB)
- `wl list --stage in_review --json` — release candidates (38 KB)
- `wl list --priority critical --status open --json` — open critical items (12 KB)
- `wl recent --number 10 --json` — recently changed (25 KB)

### 2. plan/SKILL.md line 250 (agent-facing; 383 KB worst case)

**Intent:** skip-planning heuristic — "do existing child items already cover the scope?"
**Current:** `wl list --parent <id> --json` — full records of every child.
**Alternative:** existence check `wl list --parent <id> --number 1 --json` (1.1 KB), or the canonical `wl show <id> --children --json` (already used by audit skill). No full child dump needed.

### 3. ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js lines 64, 86 (4.9 MB waste)

**Intent:** candidate items for audit-readiness / producer-review gates: `stage=in_review` OR `status=completed` (excluding `stage=done`).
**Current:** `wl list --stage in_review` (38 KB) + `wl list --status completed` (4.9 MB).
**Key insight:** per status/stage rules, `completed` pairs only with `in_review` or `done`. The code excludes `done`. Therefore `completed` minus `done` == `in_review` — **query 2 contributes zero candidates** and only re-downloads 4.9 MB of excluded items.
**Alternative:** remove the `--status completed` query entirely; keep `--stage in_review` only.

### 4. ship/scripts/check-critical-items.js line 70 (94 KB → ~16 KB)

**Intent:** gate: every critical item must be terminal (completed + in_review/done) before release; report non-terminal ones.
**Current:** `wl list --priority critical --json` (94 KB, includes years of already-terminal items), then filter in JS.
**Alternative:** query the blocking set directly — `wl list --priority critical --status open --json` + `--status in-progress` + `--status blocked` (~16 KB total). Returned items ARE the blockers; no in-script filter needed.

### 5. ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js lines 47, 65 (4.9 MB waste)

**Intent:** all items for the new CHANGELOG section (completed OR in_review).
**Current:** `wl list --status completed` (4.9 MB) + `wl list --stage in_review` (38 KB), deduped by id.
**Key insight:** same as #3 — `--status completed` adds only `stage=done` items, which are *already released* and *already in previous changelog sections*. Their inclusion is both wasteful and arguably a correctness bug (previously released items re-listed in the new section).
**Alternative:** `wl list --stage in_review --json` only (38 KB). Flag the done-item re-inclusion as a correctness question for the operator.

### 6. triage/scripts/check_or_create.py line 56 (52 KB → ~0)

**Intent:** find existing incomplete critical `test-failure` items (heuristics match test name in title/description).
**Current:** `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --json` (52 KB).
**Key insight:** heuristics only accept `open`/`in_progress` items (`_is_incomplete`), but the query returns ALL critical test-failure items — today 0 candidates exist, so every call downloads 52 KB of non-matching data.
**Alternative:** `wl list --priority critical --tags test-failure --status open --json` + `--status in-progress` (55 bytes today). Same result set, negligible payload.

### 7. code-review/scripts/create_quality_epics.py line 176 + code_review/scripts/create_quality_epics.py (duplicate; 396 KB → ~0)

**Intent:** find an existing open/in-progress epic with the exact title `Quality Improvement - Refactoring` (`issueType=epic`).
**Current:** `wl list --status open --json` (353 KB) + `wl list --status in-progress --json` (43 KB), then exact-match in Python.
**Alternative:** `wl list "Quality Improvement - Refactoring" --status open --json` + `--status in-progress` — LIKE substring on the exact known title (0 matches today → ~55 bytes each). The script's comment claims `wl search` is unreliable — but `wl list <term>` (LIKE match, full records) is the reliable, AGENTS.md-sanctioned pattern; the two were conflated.
**Note:** `code-review` and `code_review` are near-duplicate packages (differ only in invocation docstring). Fix both or consolidate — operator decision.

### 8. ship/scripts/remediate-spurious-closes.js line 81 (5.3 MB + 1,861 subprocess calls)

**Intent:** one-time historical remediation: scan ALL items' comments for spurious close reasons (`Shipped in v1.0.0` / `Shipped in v1.2.3`), delete, restore.
**Current:** `wl list` (5.3 MB) + `wl comment list <id>` for every item (~1,861 subprocess calls).
**Key insight:** FTS does not index comments, so `wl search` cannot find these strings.
**Alternative:** single `wl export --file <tmp>` + local scan/grep of the JSONL for the exact comment strings (one call, disk-based, zero context tokens). Also consider deprecating: it is a historical one-off (SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS) still referenced in ship/SKILL.md — operator decision.

### Comments/docstrings only — no action needed

- `shared/status_lifecycle.py:174`, `ship/scripts/run-release.js:271`, `audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:5260-5271`, `triage/scripts/check_or_create.py:56` (comment) — reference `wl list` only in prose/docstrings.

## Key Files

- `~/.pi/agent/skills/audit/SKILL.md` — remove bare `wl list --json` and dead `wl blocked`; scoped status commands.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/plan/SKILL.md` — `wl list --parent <id> --number 1` existence check.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — drop `--status completed` query (line 86).
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/check-critical-items.js` — query non-terminal critical statuses directly.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/release/generate-changelog.js` — drop `--status completed` query; use `--stage in_review` only.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/triage/scripts/check_or_create.py` — add `--status open` / `--status in-progress` filters.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/code-review/scripts/create_quality_epics.py` + `~/.pi/agent/skills/code_review/scripts/create_quality_epics.py` — exact-title LIKE query; dedupe decision.
- `~/.pi/agent/skills/ship/scripts/remediate-spurious-closes.js` — export + local scan; deprecation decision.
- `AGENTS.md` / `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — verify the documented `wl list` guidance covers all new patterns.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSCDR50S0066MNS` (completed) — triage helper `list_critical_issues()` ignores `wl list` results shape; same file touched here.
- `SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U` (open) — Reduce audit skill initial session context size; adjacent token-reduction goal.
- `SA-0MSL1YWOG005QAH8` (completed) — audit wastes model tokens; same theme.
- `SA-0MSITKHPW002XG4G` (completed) — duplicate static context in pi; token-reduction theme.
- `SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS` (completed) — root cause of spurious closes; context for remediate-spurious-closes.js.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Assumption:** status/stage rules are strictly enforced (`completed` ⟺ `in_review`|`done`). Verified against current data (1,638 done + 5 in_review of 1,643 completed); 6 anomalous `open/done` items exist but are not `completed` so unaffected. If the release flow ever sets other completed-stage combos, the "drop query 2" fixes must be re-validated.
- **Risk (scope creep):** code-review/code_review consolidation and remediate-script deprecation are decisions for the operator; record as separate follow-up items rather than expanding this one.
- **Risk:** changing ship gate queries could alter release behavior; mitigated by existing unit tests in `skill/ship/tests/` (scripts expose injectable boundaries) — keep test coverage green.
- **Risk:** `wl export` (23 MB) is disk-heavy; acceptable for a one-off script, not for frequent paths.
- **Assumption:** measured payload sizes are representative (worklog grows over time; relative waste ratios persist).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MQ8NQNAR009BM8Q** – Ralph Loop skill should stop once ralph loop started (completed)
- **SA-0MS9B8WDT0061G97** – Add test anti-pattern guidance to implement skill (and test-writing skills) (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `.worklog/tmp/intake-draft-wl-list-audit-SA-0MSLVQMKF000ESPZ.md` — matched: 1638, 1643, 353, agent, agents (+33 more)
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: agent, agents, already, audit, compact (+25 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: agent, agents, already, alternatives, audit (+20 more)

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: (none asked — seed intent was fully specified by the operator: iterate skills, find `wl list` uses, document intent, propose alternatives)
- A: Operator provided priority `high`. All findings derive from the repository and live worklog data (measured 2026-08-09).

## Problem

The audit runner's AC extraction (`_extract_acs` in skills/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py, ~line 1683) only recognizes markdown headings matching `^#{0,3}\s*(?:Acceptance|Success)\s+Criteria:?\s*$`. Work items whose description uses a **bold-formatted** heading such as `**Acceptance criteria:**` (e.g. NV-0MSGM4XQP007V6UM) are parsed as having **zero** acceptance criteria.

## Impact (discovered 2026-08-09 auditing NV-0MSGM4XQP007V6UM)

1. `_extract_acs` returns ['No acceptance criteria defined.'] despite 4 real ACs (AC1, AC1b, AC2, AC3) being present.
2. Phase 2 deep analysis is skipped entirely (audit_runner.py line ~4569: 'No acceptance criteria defined: skipping Phase 2 deep analysis').
3. The runner injects a hard-coded placeholder result {"text": "No acceptance criteria defined.", "verdict": "met"} (line ~4252), producing a spurious **'Ready to close: Yes'** — the item is auto-approved with NONE of its real ACs verified.

This is a false-positive approval vector: any item with a bold (non-markdown) AC heading bypasses verification entirely.

## Repro

python3 -c 'from audit_runner import _extract_acs; print(_extract_acs("**Acceptance criteria:**
- AC1: do thing"))' → ['No acceptance criteria defined.']

With `## Acceptance Criteria` heading instead → the ACs extract correctly.

## Suggested fix

Extend the heading regex (or add a pre-pass) to also match bold-formatted headings like `**Acceptance criteria:**` / `**Acceptance Criteria**` (with optional colon), and the `<<Acceptance>> <<criteria>>` angle-bracket convention already used by some work items. Add a unit test for bold headings. Also consider: when zero ACs are extracted, the runner should warn/flag rather than auto-approve.

## Verification

- `_extract_acs` extracts ACs from bold-heading descriptions.
- Re-running audit on NV-0MSGM4XQP007V6UM (or a fixture) yields per-AC verdicts instead of the placeholder.

# Problem statement

The intake skill can classify work item **type** (bug/feature/chore/task/epic) from input but has no equivalent capability for **priority** (critical/high/medium/low). This forces the agent to rely on memory or guesswork when priority is not explicitly specified by the operator.

# Users

- **AI agents** using the intake skill who need to classify work items without operator-supplied priority.
- **Operators** running `/intake` who want the skill to make intelligent judgment calls.

# Acceptance Criteria

1. A **Priority Classification** section is added to the intake skill documentation (aligned with the existing Issue Type Decision Guide).
2. The priority guide covers all four priority levels: `critical`, `high`, `medium`, `low` — with clear rules for when to use each.
3. The guide is consulted **after** operator-specified values are checked; if the operator provides `--priority` (or similar explicit flag), that value is used without classification.
4. When priority is **not** specified by the operator, the agent applies the priority classification guide to infer the correct level.
5. Existing type classification logic (Issue Type Decision Guide) remains unchanged.
6. Tests (if they exist for the intake skill) are updated or added to verify the classification logic is correct.

# Constraints

- Changes must be limited to the intake skill documentation and any related tests.
- The priority guide must be concise — consistent with the existing type decision guide's level of detail.
- Operator-specified priority/type values take absolute precedence over classification.
- The guide must be copy-paste-ready (well-formatted Markdown tables/lists).

# Existing state

The intake skill (`skill/intake/SKILL.md`) includes an **Issue Type Decision Guide** (Step 3) with:
- A Markdown table mapping each type (`bug`, `feature`, `chore`, `task`, `epic`) to use/not-use criteria and examples.
- A decision procedure (5-question flow for uncertain cases).

No priority classification exists anywhere in the skill.

# Desired change

Add a **Priority Classification** guide (table + decision procedure) to the intake skill, structured similarly to the existing type decision guide. Suggested placement: directly after the Issue Type Decision Guide in Step 3.

Suggested priority classification rules (for operator review):

| Priority | Use when… | Do NOT use when… | Examples |
|----------|-----------|-------------------|----------|
| `critical` | Security vulnerabilities, data loss, broken builds, or blocking the release pipeline | The issue is not blocking or does not involve data security/integrity | Patching a CVE, fixing CI pipeline failure, recovering from data corruption |
| `high` | Major features, important bugs, or anything blocking other work | The work is not urgent or blocking | Shipping a major feature, fixing a significant user-facing bug |
| `medium` | Default priority for standard features, enhancements, or non-blocking bugs | The issue is critical/high urgency or trivial | Regular feature development, minor bug fixes, improvements |
| `low` | Polish, minor optimizations, nice-to-have improvements | The issue affects functionality or user experience | Cosmetic fixes, minor refactoring, documentation polish |

# Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — Add Priority Classification section after Issue Type Decision Guide (Step 3)
- `skill/intake/tests/` — Update/add tests if the skill has automated verification for classification logic

# Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Classification could be wrong if the operator intended a specific priority. **Mitigation:** Operator-specified values always take precedence; classification is a fallback only.
- **Risk:** Priority classification is inherently subjective. **Mitigation:** Clear, example-driven rules reduce ambiguity.
- **Risk:** Scope creep — adding priority classification may prompt requests for similar guides on severity, risk, or effort. **Mitigation:** Record these as linked follow-up work items rather than expanding scope.

# Related work

- **SA-0MRCLNXRI0004ANE** — "Intake command: set work item type correctly (bug/feature/chore)" — Completed; established the type classification approach this work extends.
- **SA-0MSGQ47IQ00156F9** — "Add explicit issue-type categorization rules to the intake skill" — Completed; added the decision guide structure.

# Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should the priority guide mirror the exact same format as the type guide (table + decision procedure)?" — Answer: Yes, for consistency. Source: design analysis of existing type guide.
- Q: "Is there an existing priority classification anywhere that should be extended?" — Answer: No. Searched worklog and repo — no existing priority classification logic. Source: `wl search priority`, `wl search "classify priority"`.
- Q: "What priority level should this work item itself be?" — Answer: High (operator specified). Source: operator directive.

# 24h experiment: AGENTS.md STE100 instruction — session length & token use vs previous period

## Problem statement

We want empirical evidence on whether instructing agents to "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English" changes agent efficiency. Currently unmeasured. This work item runs a controlled 24-hour experiment: add the instruction to the global AGENTS.md, measure session length and token usage per session over the 24h window, compare against the previous 24h window, then revert.

## Users

- **Operator (Ralph)** — wants to know whether an STE-style output constraint affects session duration and token consumption (cost proxy) before deciding whether to adopt it permanently.

User story:
- As an operator, I want a before/after comparison of session length and token use so that I can decide whether "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." in AGENTS.md is worth keeping.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Treatment applied and verified:** `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (symlinked to `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md`) contains exactly the sentence "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." during the experiment window, and is reverted after the window. Both states verified via `grep` (before, during, after).
2. **Baseline metrics computed:** for the 24h period immediately preceding the experiment start (T0), computed from session logs for **all projects**: session count, mean/median session length (minutes), mean/median total tokens per session, input/output/cache breakdown, total tokens, and total cost where recorded.
3. **Experiment metrics computed:** same metrics for the window [T0, T0+24h), sessions attributed to the window by session start timestamp.
4. **Comparison report produced and committed:** delta % and direction for each metric (duration, total tokens, input tokens, output tokens), notable outliers (e.g. sessions with output-token-limit errors), project and model breakdown, and a one-line interpretation per metric. Report lives in the repo (e.g. `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md`).
5. **Reproducible measurement:** a single command re-runs the full analysis over the session-log directory and produces identical results (deterministic). If the measurement is delegated to the proxy's usage tooling, verify that tooling actually exists and runs; otherwise the analysis script in this repo is the source of truth (validated during intake: session logs contain per-message `usage` with input/output/cacheRead/cacheWrite/totalTokens/cost).
6. **All related documentation is updated** to reflect the changes (README/wiki entries, code comments in the analysis script).
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes** (including any tests added for the analysis script).

## Constraints

- **Bare sentence only** — the literal instruction "Always use ASD-STE100 Simplified Technical English." No rule expansion, no dictionary, no enforcement tooling.
- **Global scope** — the change lands in `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (affects every project). This is intended; the change MUST be reverted after the window.
- **Do not modify** session logs, proxy configuration, or any other project's files.
- **Measurement scope:** all sessions across all projects (per operator decision).
- STE *compliance* measurement (whether outputs actually follow STE) is **out of scope** — this experiment measures only session length and token use. Any compliance sampling should be a separate work item (scope-creep guard).
- Changes to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` follow the repo's normal workflow: implemented in a worktree, committed to `dev` (never `main`), even though this is a temporary experiment. The symlink `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md → AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` means no install step is needed; the instruction takes effect for sessions *started after* the change lands.

## Existing state

- `~/.pi/agent/AGENTS.md` is a symlink to `/home/rgardler/projects/SorraAgents/AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` (verified).
- Session logs at `~/.pi/agent/sessions/<project-slug>/*.jsonl` contain: a `session` header event (start timestamp, cwd, id) and per-message assistant events with a `usage` object (`input`, `output`, `cacheRead`, `cacheWrite`, `totalTokens`, `cost`). Last event timestamp ≈ session end. Verified during intake.
- Baseline sample (SorraAgents sessions only, 2026-08-09): 69 sessions, ~30.5h total, avg 26.6 min/session, avg 3.8M total tokens/session (dominated by cache reads; total-token values include cache). One extreme outlier session (153 min, 146.9M total tokens) associated with repeated output-token-limit errors — the report must handle such outliers (report both mean and median).
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` exists but currently contains **no source files** (only `__pycache__`). If this is the "existing usage skill in the proxy" intended for measurement, it must be verified to actually run; otherwise the analysis script in this work item is authoritative.
- `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py` measures startup-context bytes — related (our change grows startup context by ~50 bytes) but does not measure session token usage. Run before/after to confirm the addition stays within `docs/dev/context-budget.thresholds.json` if that gate is enforced.

## Desired change

1. Add the sentence to `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` in the worktree; commit to `dev`; record exact commit hash and wall-clock T0.
2. Let the experiment run 24h (T0 → T0+24h). No special agent behavior needed during the window beyond normal work.
3. At T0+24h: collect metrics for [T0−24h, T0) and [T0, T0+24h) across all projects; produce the comparison report; revert the AGENTS_GLOBAL.md change (new commit to `dev`); record revert hash.
4. Deliver: report (metrics table, deltas, outliers, interpretation), AC verification, session-log of the experiment itself.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `AGENTS_GLOBAL.md` — add then revert the STE sentence (the treatment).
- `docs/experiments/ste100-24h/report.md` — comparison report (new).
- `skill/ste100-experiment/scripts/analyze_sessions.py` (new, or revived `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/`) — deterministic analysis over `~/.pi/agent/sessions/**/*.jsonl`; produces per-session duration/tokens and window aggregates + tests.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — verify/revive if the proxy-side usage skill is to be used for measurement.

## Related work

- `SA-0MSJI53RX006E2PS` / `SA-0MSJI50Y9005VECR` — "Reduce initial LLM context…" (completed + in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`), context-budget angle. Our +1 sentence slightly increases startup context; keep within budget.
- `SA-0MSLK72KI006N9KP` (F1) — "Startup-context measurement tooling": produced `skill/context-audit/scripts/measure_context.py`; related measurement tooling, different axis.
- `SA-0MSISKM8F004NW1U` — "Reduce audit skill initial session context size": also touches startup-context surface.
- `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` — intended measurement tool per operator; source currently missing, verify.
- `SA-0MSI51QTA009WDFO` — "Add session logging instruction to AGENTS.md" (in-progress): same file (`AGENTS_GLOBAL.md`); session-traceability comments are how experiment sessions get identified/attributed.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Null result risk:** a bare STE100 sentence may not change model output measurably (no vocabulary enforcement; model may not deeply know STE rules). A null result is a valid outcome — report it as such rather than extending the experiment.
- **Confounds:** session mix (project, work type, human vs automated, model, token-limit error loops) differs between windows; day-of-week/time-of-day effects. Mitigations: report medians alongside means, break down by project/model, describe composition, keep interpretation descriptive (correlation, not causation).
- **Boundary sessions:** sessions spanning T0 or T0+24h attributed by *start timestamp* (documented rule).
- **Measurement tooling uncertainty:** if the proxy usage skill is non-functional, the repo analysis script (AC 5) is authoritative — do not block on proxy tooling.
- **Left-over instruction:** the sentence must be reverted; AC 1 greps verify both states. Add a calendar/reminder if available to avoid the window overrunning.
- **Scope creep:** STE compliance scoring, dictionary enforcement, or policy changes are separate work items (`discovered-from:SA-0MSMC8KRS00164VD` if created).

- Q2: "Measurement scope: (a) All sessions across all projects, or (b) only sessions in the project(s) whose AGENTS.md carries the instruction?" — Answer (user): "2. All (existing usage skill in the proxy will measure this)". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09. Note: intake could not locate a functional proxy usage skill — only `skill/proxy-usage-analysis/` with no source files; AC 5 requires verifying that path or falling back to the repo analysis script.
- Q3: "Instruction fidelity: keep the literal sentence only, or append a short key-rule expansion?" — Answer (user): "3. Bare sentence". Source: interactive reply 2026-08-09.

# All skills emit `</end_session>` marker on terminal state

## Problem statement

Skills currently end sessions with inconsistent closing text — some print `<work-item-id>: <summary>`, others say "This completes the <skill> process for <id>", and others produce varied output. A standardized `</end_session>` marker at the very end of every terminal skill session would make it easy for both humans and automation to detect session completion.

## Users

- **Operators (producers)** scanning session output who need a reliable visual cue that a skill has finished without pending questions.
- **Automation loops** (e.g., Ralph) that invoke skills programmatically and need a deterministic signal to detect when a skill has reached a terminal state.

### User stories

- As an operator, I want to see `</end_session>` as the last line of every skill session, so I can instantly know the skill has completed.
- As an automation system, I want to grep for `</end_session>` in a skill's output to reliably detect completion, so I don't have to parse unpredictable closing text.
- As a skill author, I want a single sentence to add as my skill's final step, so I don't have to invent my own closing convention.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] A single sentence is added as the final step to **every** work-item workflow skill in `skill/*/SKILL.md` (intake, plan, implement, audit, refactor, cleanup, ship, triage, test, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, author-command) and the report helper (`skill/report/SKILL.md` / `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py`) instructing the agent to end its terminal output with `</end_session>` on its own line. `skill/git-management` and `skill/owner-inference` are excluded — deleted in SA-0MSN81W9G006K0K8.
- [ ] The `</end_session>` marker is **not** added to helper-only skills that don't have their own session lifecycle (e.g., `speak`).
- [ ] The marker is emitted **only** when the skill reaches a terminal state without open questions for the operator — question-ended sessions (where the agent is asking for clarification) do not output the marker.
- [ ] The standardized report helper skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children: SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U, SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L, SA-0MSRFTUGH002IZE4, SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ) includes `</end_session>` as its final output line when producing a report, since it is invoked by the work-item skills.
- [ ] The existing closing conventions (e.g., implement's `<work-item-id>: <summary> / Work committed to dev`, intake's "This completes the Intake process…") are preserved **before** `</end_session>` — the marker is appended, not a replacement.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Scope:** Only work-item workflow skills listed above (not helpers like `speak`, not `command/` prompts, not the main agent loop).
- **Marker format:** Exactly `</end_session>` on its own line, as the final line of the final agent message.
- **Preserve existing output:** Skills still output their normal summary/AC/Effort-Risk content; `</end_session>` is an additional terminator, not a replacement.
- **Question-ended sessions:** If a skill session ends with unanswered questions for the operator, `</end_session>` is **not** emitted.

## Existing state

- Skills end sessions with ad-hoc closing text:
  - `skill/implement/SKILL.md`: "Close your response with: `<work-item-id>: <concise-summary>

Work committed to dev`"
  - `skill/intake/SKILL.md`: "Finish with 'This completes the Intake process for <work-item-id> <work-item-title>'"
  - `skill/plan/SKILL.md`: "End with: 'This completes the Plan process for <work-item-id>'"
- No skill currently outputs `</end_session>`.
- Related item SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S (standardize report format) is in `plan_complete` stage with 4 children; this intake is folded into that item's scope (per operator decision).

## Desired change

Add one instruction line to each work-item skill's SKILL.md final step: "End with `</end_session>`" (or equivalent phrasing that fits the skill's closing style). The `</end_session>` marker is appended after whatever closing summary the skill already produces.

## Key Files

- `skill/implement/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/intake/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to finishing step
- `skill/plan/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to final report output
- `skill/cleanup/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/test/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/triage/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/refactor/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/code-review/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/resolve-pr-comments/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/effort-and-risk/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/find-related/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/author-command/SKILL.md` — add `</end_session>` to closing step
- `skill/report/SKILL.md` — ensure report helper emits `</end_session>` as final output line
- `skill/report/scripts/render_report.py` — emits final `</end_session>` line when producing a report

> **Note:** `skill/git-management/SKILL.md` and `skill/owner-inference/SKILL.md` were listed in the original intake but were deleted in SA-0MSN81W9G006K0K8 (Retire owner-inference and git-management skills) — they are no longer in scope. Effective workflow-skill scope is now 14 files + the report helper (15).

## Related work

- **Standardize skill session end-of-session reporting via helper report skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S)** — open / plan_complete / feature. This intake is folded into that item. Children: SA-0MSRFPUTN0089F3U, SA-0MSRFTP2Y008BH6L, SA-0MSRFTUGH002IZE4, SA-0MSRFTYOI000W0IQ. The report helper skill's children are in scope for adding `</end_session>` to their final outputs.
- **Skills: tag pi sessions spawned from skills with --session-id (SA-0MSNYWMJJ002CIJ7)** — open. Tangential — session tagging, not end markers.

## Risks & assumptions

- **Scope creep risk:** Updating 16 SKILL.md files is mechanical but broad; each needs individual review to ensure the marker line fits naturally into the existing closing convention. All work-item skills are explicitly listed — no new skills added mid-flight.
- **Coordination with SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children:** The report helper skill's closing steps are defined by SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S's children; if those children are implemented before this work, their SKILL.md updates may need to include `</end_session>`. The children share this parent work item so coordination is internal to SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S.
- **Question-ended sessions:** Agents may occasionally forget to skip `</end_session>` when a question is pending. This is a soft risk — the marker is cosmetic; the real signal is workflow state.
- **Assumption:** The report helper skill (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S children) will be wired into all work-item skills and should also emit `</end_session>` when it produces a report.
- **Assumption:** `speak` is the only helper-only skill excluded (no session lifecycle). If other helpers exist without sessions, they are also excluded.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Relationship to the report-format standardization item (SA-0MSJ082OY003IQ8S)?" — Answer (operator): "(c) folded into that item as an AC / the report helper should emit the marker too." Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Scope of 'all skills'?" — Answer (operator): "(b) only work-item workflow skills — intake, plan, implement, audit, test, triage, ship, refactor, cleanup, effort-and-risk, find-related, code-review, resolve-pr-comments, git-management, owner-inference, author-command." Excludes helpers like `speak`. Source: interactive reply.
- Q: "Exact format & consumer?" — Answer (operator): "Exactly `</end_session>`, consumed by both humans and automation, only emitted on terminal state (no open questions)." Source: interactive reply.
