## Summary

The 2026-09-26 leaked-`GIT_DIR` incident (SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX) was rooted in a repository-override git environment variable exported into agent/test sessions by a launcher **outside** the `skill/` tree. Defence-in-depth now neutralises the *effect* at every in-repo execution path, but the launcher can still export a live-repo `GIT_DIR` (plus `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`) into the **pre-scrub** environment of any process that calls `git` directly. This item investigates that export and removes or scopes it at its source.

## Problem statement

On 2026-09-26 an orphaned audit fan-out inherited `GIT_DIR=<live worktree git dir>`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` and `GIT_PREFIX=` from a launcher outside the `skill/` tree. The in-repo defence-in-depth layers (shared env scrub, release-gate fail-fast, host-wide audit cap) stop that value from reaching test subprocesses, but they remain the only protection: anything spawned before the scrub that calls `git` itself can still be redirected into the live checkout. The exporting process has not been identified and no setter exists inside this repository.

## Users

- **Agent operators / maintainers** running autonomous agents through herdr/Pi: need every freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables.
- **Contributors** sharing the live checkout: need `dev`/`origin/dev` protected even when a launcher is misconfigured.

User stories:

- As an operator, I want a freshly launched agent/test session to inherit no repository-override git variables, so a misconfigured launcher can never redirect a git command into the live checkout.
- As a maintainer, I want the process that sets the override identified and fixed at source, so the defence-in-depth scrub is not the only line of protection.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] The exporting process/script is identified with reproducible, non-destructive evidence (environment of a freshly spawned agent session or a traced process ancestry), and the evidence is recorded in the work item.
- [ ] The export is removed or scoped at source so child processes — panes, `audit_runner`, `run_tests`, and direct `git` calls — never inherit a live-repo `GIT_DIR` / `GIT_WORK_TREE` / `GIT_CONFIG*`.
- [ ] A regression check asserts a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables before any git-touching step; it fails if such a variable is reintroduced.
- [ ] `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 (residual launcher risk) is updated to name the confirmed source and the fix, or to record why the source could not be confirmed.
- [ ] All related documentation is updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any relevant wiki or docs site entries.
- [ ] Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.

## Constraints

- **Non-destructive investigation.** The live checkout must never be mutated; evidence gathering must use throwaway/fixture repositories and must never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Source, not symptom.** The fix must be at the exporting launcher, not merely another in-repo scrub layer.
- **Cross-repo (Q1 = A).** The likely launcher lives in the ContextHub repository (`packages/herdr`), outside this worklog's repo. This item owns the investigation and evidence; if ContextHub is confirmed as the culprit, the code fix lands in a **linked cross-repo ContextHub work item**, not in SorraAgents.

## Existing state

Defence-in-depth landed under SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX:

- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` + `scrub_repository_overrides` / `repository_override_vars_present` / `log_repository_override_scrub`.
- `skill/test_cache.py::_default_runner`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py::_run_cmd`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py::_call_pi` pass scrubbed `env=`.
- `run_tests.py --strict-git-env` release-gate fail-fast (invoked by `.githooks/pre-push` for `dev`/`main`).
- `audit_runner.main` host-wide audit cap + `_find_orphaned_audit_processes` / `_warn_on_orphaned_audits`.
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` §9.3 documents the residual external-launcher risk.

Confirmed by search (`rg 'export GIT_|GIT_DIR='` across the repo and tooling): **no setter exists in the SorraAgents repository**. Candidate launchers identified:

- **herdr agent launcher** (ContextHub, external): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh` → `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, invoked as `herdr pane run <pane> exec bash run-pi-agent.sh <lease> ...`.
- **herdr downtime worker** (external): `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions` in `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` forwards `...process.env` to `send-to-pi.sh`, adding only `HERDR_RESOLVED_CWD` and `AUDIT_PHASE2_PARALLELISM`. It does **not** scrub repository-override vars, so a `GIT_DIR` already present in the herdr process propagates to every spawned pane.
- **git-hook chain** (in repo): `.git/hooks/post-checkout|post-merge|post-rewrite` delegate to `~/.config/pi/.githooks/worklog-post-pull` → `wl sync`. Git sets `GIT_DIR`, `GIT_EXEC_PATH` and `GIT_PREFIX` when running hooks, and `implement.py`'s `git_worktree_add` (`git worktree add`) triggers `post-checkout`. The observed `GIT_EXEC_PATH=/usr/lib/git-core` + empty `GIT_PREFIX` are the exact git-hook signature, so the poisoned environment was most plausibly inherited from a git-spawned child rather than a static shell `export`.

## Desired change

1. Determine the **origin** of `GIT_DIR` in the launcher environment — which process first set it and why — using non-destructive evidence (Q2 = C): `/proc/<pid>/environ` of pane/agent/audit processes, git `trace2` (`GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`) around `git worktree add`/hooks, launcher/hook inspection, followed by **one controlled fresh-session env dump** to prove the end-to-end state.
2. Fix at source: scrub (or refuse to propagate) `REPOSITORY_OVERRIDE_ENV_VARS` in the launcher spawn path (e.g. herdr `buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`, `run-pi-agent.sh`/`send-to-pi.sh`) and/or stop the git-hook child that leaks the variables. If the culprit is confirmed to be ContextHub/herdr, file the fix as a **linked cross-repo ContextHub work item** (Q1 = A) and note this item's remediation scope.
3. Add a regression check that a fresh agent/test session has no repository-override variables. Ownership follows Q3 = A: the in-repo SorraAgents boundary (launch wrapper / `run_tests.py`) is tested in this repo; the external launcher boundary is tested in a ContextHub test.
4. Update §9.3 with the finding and fix.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — update §9.3 with the confirmed source and fix.
- `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py` — shared override-var list/scrub helper (reuse for any in-repo mitigation or regression check).
- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — fresh-session regression check and `--strict-git-env` integration.
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — orphan/env-evidence hooks for reproducing the audit fan-out condition safely.
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — `git_worktree_add` flow that triggers the `post-checkout` hook.
- `.githooks/post-checkout`, `.githooks/post-merge`, `.githooks/post-rewrite`, `.githooks/worklog-post-pull` — hook chain (`wl sync`) executed by git with `GIT_DIR`/`GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` set.
- External (ContextHub, cross-repo — Q1 = A, fix routed to a linked ContextHub item): `packages/herdr/shared/send-to-pi.sh`, `packages/herdr/shared/run-pi-agent.sh`, `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` (`buildDowntimeSpawnOptions`).

## Related work

- **SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX** – Test/audit runner leaks GIT_DIR into test subprocesses, corrupting the live checkout and origin/dev (parent incident; completed/in_review).
- Children of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX: SA-0MUIULHQC005MUM0 (shared scrub helper), SA-0MUIUMK9Y008SCE0 (scrub in execution paths), SA-0MUIULX49001BWGG (release-gate fail-fast), SA-0MUIULC2Y009XYM1 (regression tests), SA-0MUIUMBL8002HBYH (docs + full suite), SA-0MUIUMO7T00639FL (host-wide audit cap + orphan detection).
- **SA-0MUJ2VMF7000UHCX** – Restore wl sync: main-checkout git identity was left as incident-era `T <t@t.com>` (residual incident recovery).
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (the worktree whose git dir appeared in the leaked `GIT_DIR`).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MS0DK6BD001RNDG** – implement.py abort script deletes entire project directory when aborting from main working tree (completed)
- **SA-0MUIBWORE001HOLK** – Symlink nested node_modules into implement worktrees (authoritative record for OSL-0MUFG3PJA00379CT) (completed)
- **SA-0MPAZORLO00507ZU** – The agents often run tests after commit (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0muia3oe40001qjx, 0muiumo7t00639fl, acceptable, acceptance, actual (+291 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: acceptable, acceptance, actual, add, additional (+260 more)
- `docs/dev/test-isolation.md` — matched: 0muia3oe40001qjx, 0muj2vmf7000uhcx, add, adding, agent (+241 more)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** the incident evidence (process env at the time) is gone; reproduction could itself endanger the live checkout. **Mitigation:** use a throwaway repo + `GIT_TRACE2_EVENT`; never point `GIT_DIR` at the live repo.
- **Risk:** fixing only the identified launcher leaves other propagation paths. **Mitigation:** scrub at the launcher spawn boundary (one choke point) plus the regression check.
- **Risk (scope creep):** hardening every launcher is broader than this investigation. **Mitigation:** record additional opportunities as linked work items rather than expanding this item.
- **Assumption:** the leak is architectural (environment propagation through the launcher) rather than a one-off manual `export`.
- **Assumption:** the `GIT_EXEC_PATH`/`GIT_PREFIX` signature indicates a git-spawned child origin; if tracing shows otherwise, the evidence will redirect the fix.


## Plan: changelog

- **2026-10-09**: Plan decomposition — created 5 children in test-first dependency order.
  Evidence tracing (SA-0MV0G9BF7008S01K) → controlled dump + regression test
  (SA-0MV0G9BVW008M8AT, SA-0MV0G9CD1007A0IC) → cross-repo fix
  (SA-0MV0G9CT6000LNMA) → docs update (SA-0MV0G9D960078SKT).
  Cross-repo ContextHub fix routed to linked item (per Q1 = A).
## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- **Q1 (scope / repo):** The candidate launchers are external to SorraAgents (ContextHub `packages/herdr`) and the git-hook chain that runs `wl sync`. Where should the fix land? Options: (A) investigate + evidence in SorraAgents (this item); if herdr is the culprit, file a cross-repo ContextHub work item and link it; (B) fix entirely within SorraAgents by hardening the git hooks / adding a wrapper; (C) transfer this item to ContextHub. **Recommended:** A — keeps the incident record in SorraAgents while routing the actual code change to the repo that owns the launcher. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): A.** Investigation and evidence stay in this SorraAgents item; a confirmed ContextHub/herdr culprit is fixed via a linked cross-repo work item. Source: interactive reply.
- **Q2 (reproduction):** How much live reproduction is acceptable? Options: (A) non-destructive evidence only (`/proc/<pid>/environ`, launcher/hook inspection, git trace2); (B) also spawn a live agent session and dump its env; (C) both. **Recommended:** C — trace2 + launcher inspection first, then one controlled fresh-session env dump to prove the end-to-end state. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): C.** Source: interactive reply.
- **Q3 (regression-check placement):** The AC "a freshly launched agent/test session has no repository-override variables" — where should the check live? Options: (A) an in-repo SorraAgents test of the launch wrapper/`run_tests.py`, with the external launcher covered by its own ContextHub test; (B) in-repo only; (C) ContextHub only. **Recommended:** A — each repo tests the boundary it owns. — **Answer (producer, 2026-10-08): A.** Source: interactive reply.

# Audit runner: re-auditing an in_review child demotes it and can cascade a parent block

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 (SorraAgents)
**Issue type:** bug · **Priority:** high

## Problem statement

A parent audit can silently demote children that were already `completed` /
`in_review` (and therefore exempt from the parent's child-stage and
child-verdict blocking checks) and then fail its own closure against those
demoted stages — reporting `Ready to close: No` even when every parent
acceptance criterion is `met`. On 2026-09-27, auditing
`SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63` re-screened three children whose content had changed
because the parent's commit touched files they own; each received a persisted
`Ready to close: No` child audit and was demoted (F2 →
`open`/`plan_complete`, F3 → `blocked`/`plan_complete`, F6 →
`blocked`/`plan_complete`). The parent's own verdict became `No` purely
because those children were no longer exempt, despite all six parent ACs
being `met`.

## Users and user stories

- **Audit operator** — As an audit operator, I want a parent audit to evaluate
  its own closure against the children's status as it was when the audit
  started, so an otherwise-complete parent is reported `Yes` even if a child
  is re-screened as a side effect.
- **Release manager** — As a release manager, I want a parent audit to never
  demote a completed/`in_review` child unless that child was deliberately,
  independently audited as not-ready, so a parent run cannot silently push
  completed work back into the actionable queue and cascade `blocked` states
  through the dependency chain.
- **Maintainer** — As a maintainer, I want verdicts driven only by
  unverifiable/historical or out-of-manifest ACs to be distinguishable from
  genuine code gaps, so a read-only re-audit does not downgrade an
  already-reviewed child.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. **Snapshot/exception semantics:** A children snapshot is taken at
   parent-audit start, and the parent's closure decision exempts every child
   that was in `in_review`/`done` (or otherwise exempt) at that point — even
   if the child's stage changed during the parent run. A parent whose own ACs
   are all `met`/`adjusted` is not blocked by children that were exempt at
   audit start.
2. **No side-effect demotion:** A child audit that is triggered as a side
   effect of a parent audit (the `--audit-children` cascade or the
   content-changed auto re-screen) does not change the child's lifecycle
   (`status`/`stage`) when the child was `in_review`/`done` before the parent
   run. Only a child explicitly and independently audited as not-ready may be
   demoted.
3. **No regression to genuine blocking:** A child that is in a pre-review
   stage (`idea`, `intake_complete`, `plan_complete`) or that is independently
   audited and genuinely not-ready still blocks the parent's closure. The
   existing exemption rules and the parent-first pass-through are preserved.
4. **Verdict fidelity:** ACs that are unverifiable in a read-only audit
   (historical/execution-dependent properties, or verification files outside
   the child's file-scope manifest) do not silently become blocking `partial`
   verdicts that demote an otherwise-complete item; either they are handled by
   the snapshot/no-demotion fix or they carry a distinct non-blocking
   classification.
5. **Regression test:** An automated test pins acceptance criterion 1 and 2:
   a parent audit over an `in_review` child whose only failing AC is
   unverifiable yields parent `Ready to close: Yes` and leaves the child at
   `completed`/`in_review` (or, if the chosen approach preserves the child
   stage via snapshot instead, the test asserts the parent `Yes` and the
   pre-audit child stage).
6. **Documentation:** `skill/audit/SKILL.md` and
   `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` document the child-exemption snapshot
   / no-side-effect-demotion contract, including how `--audit-children` and
   the content-changed re-screen interact with it. All related documentation is
   updated to reflect the changes, including code comments, README, and any
   relevant wiki or docs site entries.
7. **Full project test suite must pass with the new changes.**

## Constraints

- The audit remains **read-only** except the authorized persistence and
  verdict-driven status lifecycle; the fix must not add new state mutations.
- Must not weaken genuine blocking: a truly not-ready, independently audited
  child must still block its parent.
- Must preserve the existing `in_review`/`done` exemption, `inherited_pass`
  pass-through, and content-fingerprint freshness/reuse semantics.
- Keep the change surgical; prefer extracting shared logic over duplicating
  stage/verdict logic between `_has_phase1_blocking_issues` and
  `_build_issue_json`.
- Any change to child lifecycle must be consistent between the markdown
  report path (`_assemble_issue_report`) and the JSON path
  (`_build_issue_json`).

## Existing state

- `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()` and `_build_issue_json()` exempt children
  whose **current** `stage` is `in_review` (plus `status=completed` +
  `stage=done`, deleted, and `inherited_pass`). The exemption is evaluated at
  report-assembly time, against whatever stage the child holds *after* the
  parent run.
- The `--audit-children` cascade auto-triggers
  `audit_runner.py issue <child> --force`; that child run applies its own
  terminal lifecycle (`_apply_terminal_lifecycle`): a genuine `No` verdict
  transitions the child to `open`/`plan_complete` (and `wl` dependency state
  can surface it as `blocked`). The parent then evaluates its exemption
  against the demoted child stage and blocks.
- In the default parent-first flow, children whose content-fingerprint
  changed are re-screened and their audits persisted via
  `_persist_child_audit()`, which does not itself change the child stage — so
  the observed demotion originates in the cascade re-audit path.
- Unverifiable ACs (e.g. "the tests fail for behavioural reasons *before*
  F3–F5 land", or a file outside the child's file-scope manifest) fall to
  `partial`, a blocking verdict, which drives the child `No` and the
  subsequent demotion.

## Desired change

Make a parent audit non-destructive to already-exempt children and evaluate
the parent's closure against the child-exemption status captured at audit
start. Candidate mechanisms (the implementer may choose any that satisfies all
ACs, or a combination):

- **Snapshot exempt children at audit start** and evaluate the parent's
  closure against the snapshot rather than the post-re-audit stages
  (satisfies AC1).
- **Preserve a child's prior terminal stage** when a cascade-triggered child
  audit's verdict is driven only by unverifiable / out-of-manifest ACs
  (satisfies AC2, AC4).
- **Make child re-audit opt-in** so the default parent audit never mutates
  child lifecycle (satisfies AC2, complements AC1).
- **Introduce a distinct `unverifiable` verdict** for
  historical/execution-dependent ACs so they do not silently become blocking
  `partial` (satisfies AC4).

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — `_has_phase1_blocking_issues()`,
  `_build_issue_json()`, `_phase_children()` (cascade / auto-trigger),
  `_apply_terminal_lifecycle()`, `_child_content_changed()`,
  `_persist_child_audit()`, `_assemble_issue_report()`: snapshot exempt
  children at start; suppress side-effect demotion; keep markdown and JSON
  verdict paths consistent.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_review.py` — existing exemption/verdict unit tests
  (`test_child_audit_does_not_block_phase1_when_in_review`,
  `test_ready_false_when_child_audit_no`, etc.); add the regression test for
  AC5.
- `tests/test_audit_runner_core.py` — child inclusion / lifecycle tests
  (e.g. `test_completed_in_review_child_included_in_child_results`); extend
  for the snapshot/exemption behaviour.
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — Status Lifecycle + child-exemption documentation.
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — parent-first pass-through and
  `--audit-children` cascade documentation.
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — only if the fix needs to suppress or
  gate a lifecycle transition for cascade-triggered child audits.

## Risks and mitigations

- **Over-broad exemption (regression risk):** snapshotting "exempt at start"
  could let a genuinely broken child block-free if the parent started while
  the child was still `in_review`. Mitigation: keep the existing pre-review
  and independent-audit blocking paths intact (AC3) and add explicit tests
  for the pre-review block.
- **Fix only patches the parent decision, not the child demotion:** the child
  still ends up `open`/`blocked`, leaving the release queue inconsistent.
  Mitigation: treat AC1 and AC2 as jointly required, not alternatives.
- **Two divergent verdict paths:** `_build_issue_json()` and
  `_assemble_issue_report()` could drift. Mitigation: extract shared
  exemption/verdict logic and test both paths.
- **Cascade never re-audits genuinely changed children:** if re-audit becomes
  strictly opt-in, a changed child could inherit a stale pass. Mitigation:
  preserve the content-fingerprint gate so changed children are still
  surfaced, just not demoted by a parent-triggered run.
- **Scope creep:** other known audit defects (e.g.
  `SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`, `SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2`, `SA-0MU32H6KY0021SJL`) are
  related but out of scope; record them as linked work items, not scope.

## Evidence

- Parent report (all 6 ACs `met`, verdict `No`):
  `wl audit-show SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63 --json`.
- Demoted children: `SA-0MUG30HV8004HV94` (now `open`/`plan_complete`),
  `SA-0MUG30IIR00978CW` and `SA-0MUG30KEV006RBAM` (now
  `blocked`/`plan_complete`), updated at `2026-09-27T01:10:42–44Z`.

## Related work

- **SA-0MUG0WFP8008WN63** (open) — discovered-from: the parent whose audit
  exposed the bug (all parent ACs `met`, verdict `No`).
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** (completed) — "Audit runner has circular dependency
  — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage": introduced the
  `in_review` exemption this bug defeats.
- **SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0** (open) and **SA-0MUD5R5EQ000D1V2** (open) — related
  `inherited_pass` / pre-review child-stage blocking defects; coordinate to
  avoid conflicting fixes in the same exemption logic.
- **SA-0MSG9SLGI002OF7V** (completed) — precedence for "restore, never
  demote" on infrastructure-fallback verdicts; a useful pattern for the
  no-side-effect-demotion requirement.
- **SA-0MSF3RXU8005CFGD**, **SA-0MSPZDALB000S18P** (completed) — Phase 1 child
  AC review / child-verdict reuse and content-fingerprint freshness, which
  determine when a changed child is re-screened.

## Assumptions

- The fix is scope-limited to the `skill/audit` runner; no change to `wl`
  itself is required.
- Preserving the child's pre-audit stage (rather than snapshotting only the
  parent's decision) is the intended reading of AC3 — the implementer selects
  the concrete mechanism that satisfies both AC1 and AC2.
- `--audit-children` remains available for operators who explicitly want a
  full recursive re-audit; an explicit, independent child audit keeps its
  normal lifecycle.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

No clarifying questions were required: the seed work-item description already
specified the observed behaviour, the evidence (demoted child ids, parent
report), the desired behaviour, and three candidate mitigation shapes. All
related work was resolved by worklog search and repo inspection, so no
operator/producer input was needed. This intake did not ask any questions.

# [TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want regression tests that inject a **stale
`ExtensionContext`** (after a session replacement/reload) into the
`proxy-compaction-bridge` and `proxy-sse-signals` extension logic, so a stale
ctx can never crash an unrelated run and the fix is proven red-before-green.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 (stale-ctx-safe extensions)
and AC4 (Node-side regression tests that fail against pre-fix code).

## Scope

- Add `node:test` coverage that injects a stale-ctx stub whose `ui` /
  `sessionManager` accessors **throw** the pi stale-ctx error, then assert the
  extension's handler/callback behaviour is a safe no-op / context passthrough
  rather than a throw.
- Follow the existing pure-module architecture: the guard/decision helper must
  live in the dependency-free JS core (`compaction-bridge.js`,
  `sse-signals.js`) so it is importable by `tests/unit/**/*.mjs` (node v22
  cannot import the `.ts` adapters directly).
- These tests are expected to **fail against pre-fix code** (red). They will be
  made green by the two hardening implementation items.

## Acceptance Criteria

- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs` contains a case that injects a
   stale-ctx stub (getter throws on `sessionManager`/`ui` access) and asserts
   the bridge's session-scoped handling does not throw and degrades to a safe
   no-op (documented expected result).
- `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs` contains a case that injects a
   stale-ctx stub for the captured UI handle and asserts the status path does
   not throw (status write skipped/no-op).
- Running `node --test "tests/unit/**/*.mjs"` at the pre-fix commit shows the
   new cases **failing** (red evidence recorded in a work-item comment), while
   all pre-existing cases still pass.
- The new tests assert observable behaviour (no throw + no state mutation / no
   UI call), not implementation internals.

## Minimal Implementation

- Import the (new or existing) pure helper from the extension `.js` core and
  drive it with a stale-ctx stub.
- If the guard helper does not yet exist, add the test against the intended
  helper API first (red), then let the implementation item add it.

## Dependencies

- None (test-first: this item precedes the two hardening implementation items).

## Deliverables

- Added stale-ctx cases in both `tests/unit` test files.
- Red-run evidence comment on this item.

**Key Files:**
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`
- `tests/unit/test-proxy-sse-signals.mjs`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/sse-signals.js`

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-compaction-bridge against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-compaction-bridge` to no-op when
the captured `ctx` has been invalidated by a session replacement, so its
handlers never throw `This extension ctx is stale ...` and never crash or
degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`: both the
  `after_provider_response` and `context` handlers call
  `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()` — a stale ctx throws.
- Move the session-id resolution into a stale-safe helper in the dependency-free
  core `compaction-bridge.js` (e.g. `safeSessionId(ctx)` returning `null` when
  access throws). The adapter must:
  - `after_provider_response`: no-op when the session id cannot be resolved.
  - `context`: return `undefined` (pass through messages unchanged) when the
    session id cannot be resolved.
- Never let a stale-ctx throw escape a handler; never mutate dispatch on an
  unknown session.
- Update `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` to document the stale-ctx
  fail-safe behaviour.
- Preserve the compaction-bridge wire contract (LP-0MTYGZ1DI0004QP8) and the
  existing dispatch reshape semantics exactly.

## Acceptance Criteria

- With a stale-ctx stub, both handlers do not throw; `context` returns
   `undefined` (passthrough) and `after_provider_response` performs no state
   update.
- With a live ctx, behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged (existing
   compaction/reshape tests continue to pass, wire contract intact).
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md` documents the stale-ctx fail-safe
   path and this work item.
- The stale-ctx regression tests added by the test item pass (green).

## Minimal Implementation

- Add `safeSessionId(ctx)` (try/catch around `ctx.sessionManager.getSessionId()`)
  to `compaction-bridge.js` and export it.
- Use it in the two `index.ts` handlers with early return.
- Add the docs paragraph.

## Dependencies

- Depends on **[TEST] Stale-ctx regression tests for pi-client extensions**.

## Deliverables

- Stale-safe `proxy-compaction-bridge` handlers.
- Documented fail-safe behaviour.
- Green stale-ctx regression tests.

**Key Files:**
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/index.ts`
- `pi-client/proxy-compaction-bridge/compaction-bridge.js`
- `tests/unit/test_compaction-bridge.mjs`
- `docs/dev/proxy-compaction-bridge.md`

# [IMPL] Harden proxy-sse-signals against stale ctx

## Goal

As a Pi extension maintainer, I want `proxy-sse-signals` to no-op when its
captured UI handle (`statusUi`) belongs to an invalidated ctx, so a
session-replacement cannot make its async capturing-fetch callback throw and
crash or degrade an unrelated run.

Parent: **SA-0MUEIOGT2005IR7F**. Covers parent AC2 and part of AC5.

## Scope

- `pi-client/proxy-sse-signals/index.ts`: `turn_start` captures
  `ctx.hasUI ? ctx.ui : null`; the capturing-fetch callback later calls
  `statusUi.setStatus(...)` and `turn_end` calls `ctx.ui.setStatus(...)` — both
  can hit a stale ctx/UI handle.
- Add a stale-safe status helper in the dependency-free core `sse-signals.js`
  (e.g. `safeSetStatus(ui, key, text)` that swallows/guards stale-ctx throws
  and reports whether the write happened) and use it from the adapter so a
  stale handle is a silent no-op.
- `turn_end` must not throw when the ctx/UI is stale; clearing the local handle
  must still occur.
- Preserve SSE signal parsing/formatting behaviour and the passthrough of bytes
  through the capturing fetch unchanged.

  the stale-ctx fail-safe behaviour.

# Soft-deleted work items can be resurrected by status updates and re-dispatched

## Problem statement

A soft-deleted work item (one where `wl delete` has set `deletedBy`) can be resurrected via a status update, after which the downtime dispatcher re-selects it for dispatch. This caused the false-positive test-failure item SA-0MUJ14FQQ006R3PD to be worked twice after it had already been deleted.

## Users

- **Agent automation (Map, Build, etc.)**: agents rely on the downtime dispatcher to assign work and on soft-delete to permanently exclude items. Resurrection breaks this contract and wastes capacity.
- **Operator/Producer**: expects that a deleted work item will never re-appear in the dispatch queue or be worked by an agent.

## Acceptance Criteria

- **`wl update --status` refuses to change the status of a soft-deleted item.** The command checks `deletedBy` before accepting any status mutation, exits non-zero, and returns a clear error naming the deleted item.
- **`StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed` refuses to claim a soft-deleted item.** When `wl show` returns a non-empty `deletedBy`, `ensure_claimed` raises a `ClaimError` (or equivalent) instead of silently issuing a `wl update --status in-progress`. `require_claimed` also checks `deletedBy` in addition to status.
- **The downtime dispatcher excludes soft-deleted items.** The worker filters out items where `deletedBy` is set (in addition to existing `status`-based filters) at the candidate-selection stage, before the Herdr list is consumed.
- **All three guards are covered by automated tests.** Unit tests verify each refusal path; integration tests verify the dispatcher does not dispatch a soft-deleted item.

## Constraints

- The fix must be backward compatible: items already in flight at the time of the fix must not be affected.
- The `wl delete` command already sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; this fix ensures those fields are respected everywhere they matter.
- Performance impact must be negligible — each guard is a single-field check on the work-item dict returned by `wl show` or `wl list`.
- The change spans two repositories: SorraAgents (`StatusLifecycle`) and ContextHub (Worklog CLI + herdr dispatcher). Each guard is implemented, built and tested in its own repository; no single worktree spans both.

## Existing state

- `wl delete` sets `deletedBy` on the work item but **may leave the status untouched** (e.g. `open`, `in_progress`, or `completed`). Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:766`.
- `StatusLifecycle.ensure_claimed` and `require_claimed` only check `status` — they do **not** check `deletedBy`. Source: `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py:641-730`.
- The downtime dispatcher in ContextHub/herdr filters by `status === 'open'` or `status === 'blocked'` but does **not** filter by `deletedBy`. Source: `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts:6689, 6740`.
- `implement.py` already correctly skips soft-deleted children via `_is_terminal_child()`, which checks `deletedBy`. Source: `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py:761-780`.

## Desired change

Three independent guard points must be hardened:

1. **Worklog CLI**: `wl update --status` (and `wl update` generally) must reject mutations on items with non-empty `deletedBy`.
2. **Shared StatusLifecycle**: `require_claimed` and `ensure_claimed` must check `deletedBy` and refuse to operate on soft-deleted items.
3. **Downtime dispatcher**: the worker must filter out items where `deletedBy` is set, in addition to existing status filters.

**Key Files:**
- `skill/shared/status_lifecycle.py` — `require_claimed`, `ensure_claimed` methods (SorraAgents)
- `skill/shared/test_status_lifecycle.py` — unit tests for the new refusal paths (SorraAgents)
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — reference for the `_is_terminal_child` pattern (SorraAgents)
- `packages/herdr/src/downtime-worker.ts` — candidate selection and status filters (ContextHub)
- `src/commands/update.ts` — Worklog CLI `wl update` command implementation (ContextHub)

## Related work

- **SA-0MUJ14FQQ006R3PD** — the false-positive test-failure item that was resurrected (deletedBy set, then re-dispatched)
- **SA-0MUTWB8BA003J0V6** — `_is_terminal_child` correctly handles soft-deleted children in implement.py
- **SA-0MTFTFUIH000UWM9** — claim-invariant: actively worked => in_progress (related to StatusLifecycle design)

## Risks & assumptions

- **Risk:** Some agents may have already issued `wl update --status` on soft-deleted items before this fix. Mitigation: the fix only prevents future mutations; no rollback needed.
- **Risk:** The downtime dispatcher filters may exist in multiple places (candidate selection, Herdr list grouping, offer computation). All filter paths must be updated.
- **Assumption:** `deletedBy` is always non-empty string when a work item is soft-deleted (never an empty string, whitespace, or null). This is verified by inspecting the `wl delete` implementation.
- **Risk:** Adding checks in StatusLifecycle may break agents that rely on silent re-claim. Mitigation: add tests for each agent workflow that uses `StatusLifecycle`.
- **Scope creep:** This fix does not address why `wl delete` may leave status unchanged — that is a separate hygiene issue.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "Should `wl delete` also set `status=deleted` to prevent resurrection?" — Answer: No. The current convention is that `wl delete` sets `deletedBy` and `deleteReason`; status is optional to change. This fix makes `deletedBy` the authoritative gate everywhere, which is cleaner. Source: design decision from this intake.
- Q: "Does `wl delete` always set `deletedBy`?" — Answer: Yes, per the `wl delete` command implementation in the Worklog CLI. Source: code inspection.
- Q: "What about imported work items with `deletedBy` set via `wl import`?" — Answer: The audit_runner already filters these. All three new guard points will catch them uniformly. Source: `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:10769`.
data.title: Soft-deleted work items can be resurrected by status updates and re-dispatched

## Problem statement

The audit runner's automatic full-suite execution path (F3, SA-0MSTN5KRF0097TVP) calls run_cached(..., force=True) from skill/test_cache.py directly instead of going through skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py. run_cached does not acquire the shared test semaphore (TEST_MAX_CONCURRENCY / TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT) that run_tests.py uses (SA-0MTG5U75A001F1RG). Route the audit automatic suite execution through the same bounded concurrency primitive as run_tests.py (or acquire the shared test semaphore around run_cached), so audit-triggered executions cannot saturate the host or nest unbounded.

# Test groups for targeted, stage-aware testing

**Discovered-from:** SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I (R2 JSON-contract hardening). Its targeted-scope landing was blocked because the full suite now takes ~42 minutes and exceeds `.pi/test-config.json` `timeoutPerCommand=1500`.

## Problem

`run_tests.py` supports `--scope full|changed` and `--type`, but:

- `implement.py finish` falls back to the **full** suite whenever changed-scope selection is unavailable, and there is no way to run a small, meaningful group;
- the full suite now takes ~40+ minutes and exceeds the configured per-command timeout, so the finish gate times out during normal implementation;
- "changed" scope is file-based but not group-aware (an audit change should run the audit group, not the whole suite).

## Users

- **AI agents (implement phase)**: need a fast, targeted test run after each code change to iterate quickly without hitting the 1500s timeout.
- **CI system**: needs a predictable gate strategy — small groups for PR/iteration, full suite for release.
- **Producers/reviewers**: need confidence that the correct tests ran for a given change (an audit change should not be validated by running every test in the repo).

## Acceptance Criteria

1. `.pi/test-config.json` (or the project test extension) defines named test groups with their commands, and the schema is documented in `docs/dev/`.
2. `run_tests.py --group <name>` runs exactly that group; `--list-groups` lists the available groups.
3. A changed-file → group selector maps touched paths to the smallest sufficient group (e.g. `skill/audit/**` → `audit`), with a documented fallback to `full` when selection is uncertain.
4. `implement.py finish` runs the selected targeted group during iteration (build → test) so iteration no longer triggers a full-suite run, while the full group remains the gate before `dev`/`main`.
5. Per-group runtime is measured, and either the full-suite timeout is right-sized or the full group is made fast enough that `finish` completes within the configured timeout.
6. Tests cover group resolution, changed-file selection, and the fallback to `full`.
7. Full project test suite passes.

## Constraints

- UK English.
- Backwards compatible: existing `--scope full|changed` behaviour and cache keys are preserved.
- No project-specific commands hard-coded in shared tooling — groups live in project config.
- Reuse the existing test cache; groups must not create stale or mismatched cache entries.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py` — Add `--group` and `--list-groups` arguments; new group resolution logic
- `skill/test_cache.py` — Ensure cache keys are compatible with group-scoped runs
- `skill/implement/scripts/implement.py` — Wire in the targeted group selector during `finish`
- `.pi/test-config.json` — Define named groups and path→group mapping rules
- `docs/dev/` — Document the new test group schema and selector behaviour

## Risks & Assumptions

### Risks

1. **Scope creep** — Risk that the work expands to also refactor the entire `run_tests.py` test-type system. Mitigation: keep groups orthogonal to types; groups are a new dimension, not a replacement.
2. **Cache key collisions** — A group-scoped run could produce a cache entry that is later mistaken for a full-suite entry (or vice versa). Mitigation: include group name in the cache key.
3. **Changed-file ambiguity** — A single commit touching both audit and test-skill code would match multiple groups. Mitigation: select the smallest sufficient group, or require the user to disambiguate with `--group`.
4. **Full-suite timeout** — If the full suite remains >1500s, the release gate still times out. Mitigation: AC5 explicitly measures and either right-sizes the timeout or speeds up the full group.

### Assumptions

- The project's test suite is split across pytest and node — group definitions should account for both.
- The test extension mechanism (`skills_extensions/test/extension.json`) is the preferred mechanism for per-project group definitions.
- `implement.py` currently uses a hard-coded subset of logic to select changed tests; the group selector should reuse or refactor that logic rather than duplicating it.
- The default test group (when no `--group` is specified and changed-file selection is not available) is `full`, preserving existing behaviour.

## Related work

- **SA-0MU32TCFM003B78I** (R2: Harden the audit JSON contract) — This work item was discovered because R2's landing was blocked by the full-suite timeout.
- **SA-0MU2PXILZ000RPR1** — Open item about raising `timeoutPerCommand`; this work item may obviate the need for that if groups provide sufficient iteration speed.
- **SA-0MT6CENPW004V2JN** — The existing changed-file → test selector that `implement.py` uses; the group selector should build on this.
- **SA-0MUG30J5F001L57H** — `run_tests.py` live-repo snapshot guard; group-scoped runs should be compatible.
data.title: Provide targeted test groups for stage-aware testing (avoid full-suite Phase 2 timeouts)

# Ship close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done`

## Problem statement

`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` refuses
to `wl close --force <parent>` whenever *any* descendant is not itself in the
close-candidate set (candidates come only from `getCandidateItems()`, which
returns `stage: in_review` items). Descendants that are already terminal
(`stage: done` / `status: deleted`) therefore look like "collateral" and
falsely block the parent's close, even though a terminal child needs no
action. This was observed during the ContextHub v1.0.16 release, where the
auto-close step closed **0 of 14** released `in_review` items.

## Users and user stories

- **Primary user — release producer/operator.** As the producer running a
  release, I want the post-release close step to close a released parent whose
  only non-candidate descendants are already terminal, so I do not have to
  force-close it by hand or leave released work in `in_review`.
- **Secondary user — the ship pipeline.** As `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, I
  want a correct, non-sweeping scope signal: terminal descendants are
  harmless, genuinely non-terminal descendants must still block, and a
  descendant held back for producer review should be reported as such.
- **Secondary user — audit/release operators.** As an operator reading the
  release log, I want the refusal reason to name the *real* cause (e.g.
  `needsProducerReview`), not a generic collateral list, so I know what to do
  next.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. The collateral-exclusion set excludes descendants that are already terminal
   (`stage: done` or `status: deleted`), so a parent whose only non-candidate
   descendants are terminal is closed. *(Core defect — already implemented by
   sibling `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`, commit `9c9d55b9`; keep and verify.)*
2. A descendant skipped solely because `needsProducerReview=true` is reported
   with a **distinct** refusal reason (not lumped under the generic
   "collateral" list), while the parent is still refused. *(Remaining work.)*
3. Genuine non-terminal descendants (`open`/`blocked`/`in_progress`/
   `intake_complete`/`plan_complete`) still block the parent close — the scope
   guard must not be weakened. *(Already implemented; keep and verify.)*
4. Regression tests with injected `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/
   `getItemLifecycleFn` cover: (a) all-done descendants → parent closes;
   (b) one non-terminal descendant → parent refused; (c) an npr=true
   descendant → parent refused with a distinct reason. (a) and (b) exist;
   (c) is missing. *(Remaining work.)*
5. `npm run build` and all existing suites pass.
6. All related documentation (release-process docs and ship/audit skill
   references) reflects the distinct `needsProducerReview` refusal reporting.

## Constraints

- Minimal, additive change to `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`; do not weaken the
  out-of-scope scope guard (`SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H AC9/AC10`).
- Do not change the existing child producer-review override/absorption logic
  (`SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q`).
- Unit tests must inject fakes and must never mutate the live worklog
  (`SA-0MSJ2XMQL006CVQS`).
- Follow build → test → commit order; never commit with a failing suite.

## Existing state

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` already filters terminal descendants out of the
  collateral set (~lines 541-559), added by **`SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`**
  ("Ship close terminal-descendant exclusion", commit `9c9d55b9`, on `dev`) as
  defence-in-depth for `SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP` (cascade descendants of an
  audit-approved parent). AC1 and AC3 are therefore already satisfied.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` already covers
  (a) all-terminal descendants → close, (b) non-terminal descendant → refuse,
  and a mixed terminal/non-terminal case; all 23 tests pass. AC4(c) is absent.
- AC2 (distinct `needsProducerReview` refusal reporting) is **not**
  implemented: the refusal reason at ~line 561 is
  `Refused: --force close would sweep descendant(s) outside the candidate set: …`
  regardless of cause.
- The cascade policy (`SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP`, completed) makes fully-terminal
  subtrees common, further reducing the original false-refusal occurrence.
- Related but distinct: `SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5` (ship release must *verify*
  in-scope items were actually closed — open).

## Desired change

1. In `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease`, classify a non-candidate, non-terminal
   descendant that is held back solely because `needsProducerReview=true`
   separately from generic collateral, and surface a distinct refusal reason
   (the parent is still refused).
2. Add the AC4(c) regression test asserting the distinct reason.
3. Update the relevant release/ship documentation for the new reporting.
4. Re-verify AC1/AC3 by running the existing terminal-descendant tests and
   `npm run build`.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` collateral
  classification and refusal-reason construction (~lines 530-575); add the
  distinct npr classification.
- `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs` — add the AC4(c)
  npr=true descendant test.
- `docs/dev/release-process.md` (and/or the ship/audit skill reference docs) —
  document the distinct `needsProducerReview` refusal reporting.

## Risks and assumptions

- **Assumption:** the core false-refusal (AC1/AC3) is already fixed on `dev`
  by `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9` (commit `9c9d55b9`) and its tests pass, so the
  residual scope is AC2 + AC4(c) + verification. *If the producer disagrees,
  re-scope or close the item (see Appendix OPEN QUESTION).*
- **Risk — scope guard regression (medium):** touching the collateral
  classification could accidentally let genuinely non-terminal descendants be
  swept by `wl close --force`. **Mitigation:** keep AC3 covered by the existing
  non-terminal refusal tests and add the AC4(c) case without relaxing AC3.
- **Risk — over-broad npr reporting (low):** classifying *all*
  `needsProducerReview` descendants as a distinct reason could mislabel ones
  that are candidates/terminal. **Mitigation:** classify only non-candidate,
  non-terminal descendants held back solely by `needsProducerReview`.
- **Risk — documentation drift (low):** release docs may already describe the
  terminal exclusion but not the distinct npr reason. **Mitigation:** AC6
  explicitly updates the docs.
- **Scope-creep guard:** the broader out-of-scope/parent-coverage themes
  (`SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H`) and the `inherited_pass` tracking-hygiene issue
  (`SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`) are **out of scope** here and remain tracked by
  their own items.

## Related work

- **`SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`** (completed) — terminal-descendant exclusion;
  already implemented AC1/AC3 of this item.
- **`SA-0MUR7Y3BJ004FGPP`** (completed) — cascade children of an
  audit-approved parent to `completed`/`done` (the producer's stated policy
  and the root-cause counterpart).
- **`SA-0MUJLWPB10038Z8Q`** (completed) — override/absorb
  `needsProducerReview` on children of a release-ready parent.
- **`SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H`** (completed) — parent-coverage / out-of-scope rules
  for child audits (the scope guard being preserved).
- **`SA-0MUA4Q431008HIH0`** — audit runner `inherited_pass` bypasses the
  children-stage block (related tracking-hygiene concern).
- **`SA-0MUXA5ZNZ0019QY5`** (open) — ship release must verify in-scope items
  are actually closed before reporting success.

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

- Q: "The core false-refusal (AC1/AC3) is already implemented by
  `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9` and all existing tests pass. Should this item remain
  open for the residual `needsProducerReview` distinct-reporting scope
  (AC2/AC4c), or be closed as substantially resolved?"
  — **OPEN QUESTION (non-blocking assumption applied).**
  **Recommended:** keep this item open and narrow the remaining work to AC2
  (distinct npr refusal reason) + AC4(c) (regression test) + verification.
  Rationale: the item's author explicitly listed AC2/AC4(c) as desired
  behaviour, and the sibling work item records this item as "the primary/
  broader ship-side item". Answer: *assumed keep-open/narrow* by Map; producer
  may re-scope or close. Source: work-item descriptions of
  `SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP` and `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`; code inspection of
  `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` and
  `tests/unit/test-close-work-items-after-release.mjs`.

- Q: "Is the `needsProducerReview` descendant actually reachable as a
  collateral refusal?"
  — Answer: yes (research finding). A descendant with
  `needsProducerReview=true` in `stage: in_review` is a candidate; if it is
  **not** covered by an audit-ready ancestor it is skipped rather than closed,
  so it is absent from `toClose`/`candidateIds` and lands in the generic
  collateral set. Source: code inspection of
  `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`).

- Q: "Could the terminal-descendant fix have removed the need for this item
  entirely?"
  — Answer: no. `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9` addressed only the terminal-descendant
  false positive (AC1/AC3); AC2 distinct reporting and AC4(c) remain, as does
  the high-priority release-blocking symptom. Source: `SA-0MUTYRYUG008A4A9`
  AC1-AC3 and its description of this item as the primary/broader item.
## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MPG1X6M2005CKKT** – Ralph stream hangs when pi never closes stdout (completed)
- **SA-0MSRWB5LM0057VQ9** – [test-failure] closes work items ONLY after the merge is verified — failing test (completed)
- **SA-0MRPL5WLZ000JZ9V** – Related Items is too broad (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched: 0mu2oy1n9000xl2h, 0mua4q431008hih0, 0mur7y3bj004fgpp, absent, ac1 (+244 more)
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched: 0mu2oy1n9000xl2h, 0mua4q431008hih0, 0mujkpdaa002vvdp, 0mur7y3bj004fgpp, absent (+232 more)
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched: 0mu2oy1n9000xl2h, 0mur7y3bj004fgpp, absent, ac2, ac3 (+207 more)

# Ship skill: let a release-ready parent override (or absorb) `needsProducerReview` on its children

## Problem statement

The ship release close step (`closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` in `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) skips every item with `needsProducerReview === true`:

```js
const toClose = items.filter((item) => item.needsProducerReview === false);
```

For a **child** item flagged `needsProducerReview=true`, this leaves the child in `in_review`; because `wl close --force` is then refused (to avoid sweeping a non-candidate descendant), the **parent** is refused too and remains un-closed in tracking even though the code has shipped.

### Motivating case (ContextHub v1.0.16)

- Parent `WL-0MU87ZGPP0029V28` (`in_review`, audit passed, code on `main`) has 5 children.
- 4 children were closed; the 5th, `WL-0MU8807BI008C9ME`, is `in_review` with `needsProducerReview=true`.
- Result: the parent cannot be closed and remains `in_review` despite shipping. Every other blocker was resolved.

The existing scoping rules (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H) already say a child's audit/review is **covered by an audit-ready `in_review` parent** — so a covered child's `needsProducerReview` flag should not outlive, nor contradict, that parent's ready-to-release determination.

## Users

- **Release manager / release agent:** wants a release-ready parent to be closeable without being blocked by a covered child's stale `needsProducerReview` flag; the release record should reflect what actually shipped.
- **Producer:** must keep a real veto — if a child genuinely needs producer attention, the flag must escalate up and block the release rather than be silently cleared.
- **Auditor / future agent:** needs every flag mutation to be logged with the authorising parent/audit so the override is auditable.

Example user stories:

- As a release manager, when a child is covered by an audit-ready `in_review` parent, I want its `needsProducerReview` flag cleared (with an explanatory comment) and the child closed, so the parent can be closed after release.
- As a producer, when a child that genuinely needs my attention would otherwise be swept, I want the parent flagged `needsProducerReview=true` with the child id(s) enumerated, so the release is blocked until I approve.
- As an operator running `--dry-run`, I want the planned overrides/escalations reported with no worklog mutations.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. A child with `needsProducerReview=true` under an audit-ready `in_review` parent is closed after its flag is cleared, with an explanatory comment on the child.
2. A child that genuinely needs attention causes the parent to be flagged `needsProducerReview=true` with a comment naming the child(ren); the parent then fails the producer-review gate.
3. Clearing a child flag is refused when the parent is not `in_review` or its audit is not `readyToClose`.
4. `--dry-run` performs no mutations and reports the intended child overrides and parent escalations.
5. Unit tests inject `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/`runCloseCommand` boundaries and never mutate the live worklog.
6. `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` and `SKILL.md` document the override/escalation contract.
7. `npm run build` and existing suites pass.

## Desired change

When the release skill evaluates a **child** with `needsProducerReview=true`, it must resolve the flag against the parent's readiness:

1. **Parent overrides (default when the parent is release-ready):** if the child's nearest `in_review` ancestor is an audit-ready release candidate (`readyToClose === true`), the skill may **clear the child's `needsProducerReview` flag** (set `false`) and record a comment on the child explaining the override, then close it. The parent's passing audit is what authorises the override.
2. **Genuine attention required:** if the child genuinely needs producer attention (unresolved question, ambiguous requirement, manual approval owed), the skill must **escalate to the parent** instead: set `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent and add a comment **enumerating the child id(s)** that require attention. The parent then blocks the release through the existing producer-review gate (Step 3.6) — the correct fail-safe.
3. The override must **never** be authorised by status alone: it requires the parent's passing audit (`readyToClose === true`). A non-`in_review` parent or an unaudited parent must not silently clear a child flag.
4. Every flag change (child cleared, or parent escalated) must be **logged** with a comment naming the authorising parent/audit or the children that need attention.
5. `--dry-run` must report the planned overrides/escalations without mutating any work item.

## Existing state

- `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()` (`skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js`) filters candidates to `needsProducerReview === false`, then refuses any candidate whose `--force` close would sweep descendants outside the candidate set (`candidateIds`), reporting them as `refusedItems` (SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H AC9/AC10). This is the mechanism that leaves a parent un-closed when a child is skipped.
- `getCandidateItems()` (`skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js`) projects only `{id, title, needsProducerReview, parentId}` from `wl list --stage in_review` — it does not carry audit state.
- The producer-review gate (Step 3.6, `checkProducerReviewStatus`) is scoped to **top-level** candidates via `getTopLevelCandidateItems()`; children never block it.
- The final-validation sweep (Step 3.7, `check-final-validation.js`) already resolves child scope: a child whose nearest `in_review` ancestor has a passing audit (`readyToClose === true`) is `covered` and skipped; a child with no audit-ready `in_review` ancestor is `uncovered` and blocks if it has a missing/stale/failing audit or `needsProducerReview === true`. It can inject `getItemsFn`, `runAuditShow`, `runAuditCommand`, `resolveAuditRunnerFn`.
- The close step runs **after** the release has merged (Step 11, gated by `verifyReleaseMerge()`); Steps 3.6/3.7 run **before** the merge.

## Constraints

- The override must be authorised only by an audit-ready `in_review` parent (`readyToClose === true`); never by status alone.
- `--dry-run` must remain mutation-free.
- Unit tests must be hermetic (no live `wl`/audit-runner calls, no live worklog mutation).
- Changes are confined to the ship skill (`skill/ship/scripts/`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`) and `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md`.
- Preserve existing behaviour for top-level items and for genuinely-flagged uncovered children.

## Key Files (predicted)

- `skill/ship/scripts/run-release.js` — `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease()`: add child-flag resolution (override vs escalate), comments, and `--dry-run` reporting; pass through new injectable boundaries.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-audit-gate.js` — possibly extend `getCandidateItems()` projection (e.g. carry `parentId` already present) and/or add an ancestor/audit resolver used by the close step.
- `skill/ship/scripts/check-final-validation.js` — likely the pre-ship home of the escalation half of the contract (see Open Question 1).
- `skill/ship/tests/` — new hermetic unit tests for override, escalation, refusal, and `--dry-run` (there is currently only `test_discord_notify.mjs`).
- `docs/dev/ship-skill-reference.md` — document the override/escalation contract and close-step behaviour.
- `skill/ship/SKILL.md` — document the override/escalation contract.

## Risks and assumptions

- **R1 — Escalation timing:** if escalation (case 2) runs only in the post-ship close step, setting `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent cannot block *this* release (Steps 3.6/3.7 have already passed). It would only affect the next release. Resolving this is Open Question 1.
- **R2 — Missing audit data in the close step:** the close step's candidate projection has no `readyToClose`, so it cannot currently authorise an override. A new injectable boundary is likely required (Open Question 2); AC5's stated boundary list may be incomplete.
- **R3 — Overriding a producer's explicit signal:** clearing `needsProducerReview=true` mutates a human-set signal. The contract relies on the parent's passing audit as the authorising evidence and on a mandatory comment for traceability (Open Question 3).
- **R4 — Scope creep:** additional improvements (e.g. a general ancestor-audit cache, change to the Step 3.6/3.7 ordering) are recorded as separate work items, not folded into this one.
- **Assumption:** the "nearest `in_review` ancestor" walk semantics match the existing final-validation coverage walk (skip non-`in_review` / non-passing ancestors, continue up the chain, break cycles conservatively).

## Related work

- SA-0MU2OY1N9000XL2H — parent-coverage / out-of-scope child rules for child audits in the final-validation gate (completed, `in_review`).
- SA-0MUJKPDAA002VVDP — close step falsely refuses to close released items whose descendants are already `stage=done` (open). Complementary: that item stops refusing on already-done descendants; this item resolves the `needsProducerReview` child case.
- SA-0MS21B5MP004AUUS — close work items after release only when `readyToClose` and producerReview conditions are met (completed). Origin of the producer-review gating and the close-step filter.
- SA-0MS4TXDPG003OFYO — filter `closeWorkItemsAfterRelease` by `needsProducerReview` (completed). The behaviour being refined.
- SA-0MS4TJR2R0043UHO — extend `getCandidateItems` and add `checkProducerReviewStatus` (completed).

## Related work (automated report)

### Related work items
- **SA-0MSKB6WA8009XKTX** – Audit: refresh measured baseline and performance docs (completed)
- **SA-0MRW0G0XZ009TU6E** – [CRITICAL] Audit runner has circular dependency — child audit verdict blocks parent regardless of stage (completed)
- **SA-0MLQ8YP2X0I2XJ0M** – Prerequisite Validation and Error Handling (completed)

### Repository file matches
- `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` — matched on the terms shared with this brief package (audit, ancestor, approval, child, close, producer, ready, …).
- `docs/dev/audit-skill-reference.md` — matched on the terms shared with this brief package (acceptance, ancestor, child, producer, ready, …).
- `skill/audit/SKILL.md` — matched on the terms shared with this brief package (ambiguous, ancestor, child, needsproducerreview, producer, …).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (OPEN QUESTION) — Where does the child→parent **escalation** (contract case 2) execute? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790506262-3754936-23077`)
- **Context:** The close step (Step 11) runs *after* the release has merged; the producer-review gate (Step 3.6) and final-validation sweep (Step 3.7) run *before*. The brief says setting `needsProducerReview=true` on the parent makes it "fail the producer-review gate", which is impossible if performed at close time for the current release.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** implement escalation in the **pre-ship final-validation sweep (Step 3.7)**: when an *uncovered* child has `needsProducerReview=true` and no audit-ready `in_review` ancestor, set the flag on the nearest `in_review` ancestor (or top-level parent) with a comment enumerating the child(ren), so the gate blocks *before* shipping. The close step then only performs overrides for covered children.
- **Alternative A:** implement everything in the post-ship close step; escalation only affects the *next* release (does not fail the current producer-review gate).
- **Alternative B:** both — escalate pre-ship in Step 3.7 and re-assert in the close step.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — pending producer decision._

### Q2 (OPEN QUESTION) — How does the close step learn an ancestor's `readyToClose` (and is AC5's boundary list complete)? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790506262-3754936-23077`)
- **Context:** `getCandidateItems()` projects only `{id, title, needsProducerReview, parentId}` — no audit state. AC5 names only `getCandidateItemsFn`/`getDescendantsFn`/`runCloseCommand` as injectable boundaries, which is insufficient to resolve an ancestor's audit without a live call.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** add an injectable boundary (e.g. `getAncestorStatusFn` / `getParentAuditFn`) that resolves the nearest `in_review` ancestor and its audit verdict, defaulting to a `wl show` + `wl audit-show` query; extend AC5 accordingly. Keeps tests hermetic.
- **Alternative A:** derive a parent map from `getCandidateItemsFn()` alone — insufficient, because a non-candidate/unaudited ancestor is not present in the candidate list.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — pending producer decision._

### Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — Is clearing a producer-set flag authorised by the parent's passing audit alone, or does it need an explicit opt-in? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790506262-3754936-23077`)
- **Context:** `needsProducerReview=true` is a human/producer signal. Desired-behaviour item 3 says the parent's `readyToClose === true` audit is the authorisation; desired-behaviour item 4 requires a comment. AC3 only forbids authorising by status alone.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** override is authorised solely by the parent's passing audit (`readyToClose === true`) plus a mandatory explanatory comment naming the authorising parent/audit id — matching desired behaviour items 3 and 4 as written.
- **Alternative A:** require an explicit release-command opt-in (e.g. `--override-child-producer-review`) before any child flag may be cleared.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — pending producer decision._

data.description:
`wl sync` overwrites a locally-persisted audit result with an older copy, silently reverting a just-written audit (data loss / audit-record corruption).

## Problem

When a `wl sync` runs after a local audit has been persisted (via the canonical audit persister / `wl audit-set`), the locally written audit text is replaced by an older copy of the audit. The item's other fields (status, stage, `needsProducerReview`, comments, description) are preserved, so the store is left internally inconsistent: the lifecycle reflects the new verdict while the stored audit shows a stale verdict.

Observed 2026-09-26 on `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` in the LLM project (`/home/rgardler/projects/llm`):

1. The audit runner persisted a new `Ready to close: No` audit at `2026-09-26T13:34:32.382Z`; `wl audit-show` read it back immediately (verified).
2. A herdr-scheduled `wl sync` ran (`.worklog/last-sync-time` advanced to `2026-09-26T13:38:00Z`); afterwards `wl audit-show` returned the **old** `2026-08-15T12:59:45.425Z` `Ready to close: Yes` audit.
3. Re-persisted via `persist_audit.py` at `2026-09-26T13:37:27.757Z`; a further `wl sync` reverted it again.
4. Re-persisted once more at `2026-09-26T13:39:21.882Z` (no sync running); it remained stable while no sync ran.

The item's status/stage (`open`/`plan_complete`) and its comments (including ones added after the new audit) survived each sync — only the audit text reverted.

## Evidence

- The synced export `refs/worklog/remotes/origin/worklog/data:.worklog/worklog-data.jsonl` contains only `workitem` and `comment` records — **no audit field/record at all** (`grep -c '<new-fingerprint>' worklog-data.jsonl` → 0; the `workitem` record keys do not include `audit`).
- Therefore the audit cannot be propagating through the git sync export, yet the old audit reappears after sync — suggesting the audit is not carried by the export and the sync restores/keeps an older audit from another source, or the merge drops local-only audit changes.
- Commands used: `wl audit-show <id> --json`, `persist_audit.py --issue-id <id> --file <report>`, `git for-each-ref refs/worklog/...`, `.worklog/last-sync-time`.
- Worklog prefix: `SA` (this repo). The affected store was `LP` (LLM project).

## Impact

- Audits persisted by the canonical audit runner can be silently reverted, leaving `status`/`stage` inconsistent with the stored audit text (e.g. item demoted to `open`/`plan_complete` while `audit-show` reports a stale `Yes`).
- Operators and orchestrators reading `wl audit-show` can be misled about whether an item is ready to close.
- Concurrent syncs (herdr-scheduled) make the loss deterministic during busy periods, so re-persisting does not reliably fix it.

## Expected behaviour

- A `wl sync` must never downgrade a newer locally-persisted audit to an older one. Merge semantics for audit text should be last-write-wins by audit time (or audits should be excluded from sync-triggered overwrites until pushed).
- If the sync cannot carry audit text in the git export, it must leave the local audit untouched rather than reverting it.

## Acceptance Criteria

1. Reproduce in a test: persist audit A (older), then a newer audit B on the same item, run the sync/merge path, and assert `wl audit-show` returns B (not A).
2. The synced worklog export either carries audit records/fields, or the sync merge explicitly preserves the newest local audit (documented decision).
3. A sync that cannot represent audits leaves the local audit unchanged (no revert).
4. Regression fixture uses two audits with distinct `auditedAt` timestamps and the real sync export/import path.
5. Existing worklog sync tests pass.

## Notes

- Discovered during the audit of `LP-0MSPZUD4G007IYGH` (proxy usage analysis fast/cheap bucketing). Recording it here as instructed by the operator; out of scope for that audit.
- Related: audit persistence ordering contract (comments before persistence), and the audit freshness gate — a reverted audit text also makes the content-fingerprint freshness gate evaluate against the wrong (older) report.

## Summary

The audit runner's Phase 2 FILE SCOPE manifest omits the audited item's **committed** touched files whenever the working tree is clean, causing false "outside the manifest" / `unmet` verdicts for criteria whose implementation and tests live in those committed files.

Discovered during the audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (log: `~/.audit_debug/SorraAgents/audit_run_SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX_20260927T095408.log`).

## Evidence

- The audit of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX returned `Ready to close: No` with parent AC1 `partial`, AC2 `unmet`, AC3 `unmet` — each justified by wording such as "`test_cache._default_runner`/`run_tests.py` are outside the provided manifest" and "test_cache is outside the manifest so its runner cannot be verified".
- The item's implementation commit `a83ada6a` changed 14 files (`git show --stat a83ada6a`): `.githooks/pre-push`, `docs/dev/test-isolation.md`, `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py`, `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_concurrency.py`, `skill/shared/git_sandbox.py`, `skill/shared/tests/test_git_sandbox.py`, `skill/ship/SKILL.md`, `skill/test/scripts/run_tests.py`, `skill/test_cache.py`, `skill/test_runner.py`, `tests/test_implement_sys_path_resolution.py`, `tests/test_repository_override_isolation.py`, `tests/test_run_tests_cache.py`.
- `git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX --name-only` returns all of those files, so the data is available — the manifest simply did not use it.
- The manifest actually used contained only `skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py` and `skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py`; the latter is **not** in `a83ada6a`.
- The working tree was clean at audit time (`git status --porcelain` showed only `.worklog/scheduled-prompts.json`).

## Root cause

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` (`skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py:4351`) builds the manifest's file list from:

1. the description's Key Files (`_extract_key_files`);
2. `_git_changed_files()` (`audit_runner.py:4210`) — `git diff --name-only HEAD` plus `git status --porcelain=v1`, i.e. **working-tree / untracked changes only**;
3. Phase 1 evidence `file:line` refs;
4. a lightweight repo index.

It does **not** use `_resolve_touched_files()` (`audit_runner.py:1476`), which already resolves the union of (a) files in commits referencing the item id (`git log --all --fixed-strings --grep=<id> --name-only`), (b) comment-recorded commit hashes, and (c) Key Files — the correct source for a fully-committed item on a clean checkout.

Consequently, when an item's work is committed and the tree is clean (the normal post-implementation state), `_git_changed_files()` contributes nothing and the manifest collapses to the Phase 1 evidence refs + repo index. The `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` fail-fast guard (`audit_runner.py:1231`) does not abort because the manifest does reference *some* item-repo file, even though it omits the item's actual touched files.

## Desired behaviour

`_build_file_scope_manifest()` must include the audited item's committed touched files (via `_resolve_touched_files()`), so a clean checkout still yields a manifest covering the item's real changes. The fail-fast scope validation must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] `_build_file_scope_manifest()` includes the audited item's committed touched files (reuse `_resolve_touched_files()`), in addition to the working-tree diff, Key Files, Phase 1 refs, and repo index.
- [ ] Regression test: with a clean working tree and a committed commit whose message references the item id, the built manifest contains that commit's changed files.
- [ ] A scope-validation regression test asserts that a manifest which references the item repo but omits the item's touched files is rejected (or is impossible to build).
- [ ] Re-auditing SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX after this fix no longer reports its ACs as "outside the manifest" solely because the item's files are committed rather than uncommitted.
- [ ] Full suite green.

## Key Files (predicted)

- skill/audit/scripts/audit_runner.py — `_build_file_scope_manifest`, `_git_changed_files`, `_resolve_touched_files`, `_validate_file_scope_manifest`
- skill/audit/tests/test_audit_runner_core.py

## Related work

- discovered-from:SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX — the audit whose false-negative verdicts surfaced this defect.
- Blocks the accurate re-audit/closure of SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX (dependency edge recorded).

## Appendix: Clarifying questions & answers

### Q1 (RESOLVED) — Does AC3 require hardening `_validate_file_scope_manifest()`, or is the "impossible to build" regression test sufficient? (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** AC3 says a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files must be "rejected (or is impossible to build)". The Desired-behaviour section separately states the fail-fast scope validation "must not accept a manifest that references the item repo but omits the item's touched files", which reads as a validator-hardening requirement.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** harden `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` with an optional `touched_files` argument: when a non-empty touched set is resolvable and none of its paths appear in the manifest, return a scope error; when the set is `None`/empty, fail open (preserves current behaviour for mono-repo/unknown cases). Plan child SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O covers this; the regression test is delivered either way.
- **Alternative A:** satisfy AC3 solely with the "impossible to build" regression test (no validator change).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **harden**. `_validate_file_scope_manifest()` gains an optional `touched_files` argument that returns a scope error when a non-empty resolved touched set has no path in the manifest, and fails open when the set is `None`/empty. Delivered by SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O; the regression test is still required.

### Q2 (RESOLVED) — The item's `effort`/`risk` fields are lowercase ("medium"/"medium"), so the plan-approval gate's documented Medium-effort trigger did not fire. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `should_request_plan_approval()` compares `effort` case-sensitively against `{"Medium", "Large", "Extra Large"}`. `wl show` reports this item's values as `"medium"`/`"medium"` (other items, e.g. SA-0MUIA3OE40001QJX, use `"Medium"`/`"Severe"`). `plan_helpers.py plan-approval-gate` therefore returned `request_approval: false`, skipping the human checkpoint the skill documents for Medium effort.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** correct the item's `effort`/`risk` to canonical capitalised values and, if plan sign-off is wanted, review the child breakdown before implementation. (Making the gate case-insensitive is a separate change, out of scope here.)
- **Alternative A:** accept the gate result as-is and proceed without a producer approval pause (what this run did).
- **Answer:** ACCEPTED (producer, 2026-09-27): **correct**. The item's `effort`/`risk` were set to the canonical capitalised values (`Medium`/`Medium`) via `wl update`. With the corrected data, `plan-approval-gate` returns `request_approval: true` ("its effort is Medium scale"), so the plan is surfaced to the producer for sign-off before implementation.

### Q3 (OPEN QUESTION) — `extract_acceptance_criteria()` only exits the AC section on an `##` heading, so an H1-headed description makes the AC-coverage review treat Key Files / Related-work bullets as ACs and recommend `stop`. (raised by Map, session `herdr-1790545473-1902849-18949`)
- **Context:** `skill/shared/tree_coverage.py::extract_acceptance_criteria` detects the AC header with `^#+\s+Acceptance\s+Criteria` but breaks only on `^##\s+`. This plan normalised this item's and its children's headings to `##` (conformant with the AGENTS.md `## Acceptance Criteria` convention) so coverage parses correctly. Tracked as discovered-from work item SA-0MUKCQ4TL0075WZJ.
- **Preferred option (recommended):** reaffirm the H2 convention for descriptions and make the extractor break on any heading level 1–6 for robustness.
- **Answer:** _OPEN — informational; no plan decision depends on it._

### Plan approval (2026-09-27)

- **Decision:** APPROVED — producer replied "LGTM" to the four-child, test-first plan (SA-0MUKCOQI10095463 → SA-0MUKCOUXN001VH47 → SA-0MUKCOW1I001MJ7O → SA-0MUKCOX3T0057ES6). The plan-approval gate (Medium effort) is satisfied; `needsProducerReview` is cleared and the plan is ready for implementation.
data.title: Audit FILE SCOPE manifest omits a clean tree's committed touched files, causing false out-of-scope verdicts

## Summary
On a shared host with several agents running implement/test/audit concurrently, the full suite produced environment-induced failures with no code defect:

1. `tests/test_live_repo_mutation_guard.py::TestRunTestsGuardFires::*` and
   `tests/test_pytest_path_resolution.py::test_run_tests_spawns_resolved_pytest_when_missing`
   fail with `subprocess.TimeoutExpired ... timed out after 180 seconds`: the nested
   `run_tests.py --scope full` invocation waits for the host-wide "test" semaphore
   (max 2) and exceeds the spawning test's 180 s subprocess timeout.
2. The `live_repo_guard` plugin reports "live-repo mutation detected" at teardown
   when **other agents** push to `origin` (observed `refs/remotes/origin/dev` and
   `refs/heads/wl-*` moving mid-run), even though the suite itself did not mutate
   the checkout.

## Evidence
- SA-0MSN2LIOQ004TON1 validation: an armed full run gave 3249 passed / 0 failures
  with 3 guard teardown errors; another armed run gave 3246 passed / 3 failures
  (two nested-runner 180 s timeouts + one path-resolution timeout); a run with the
  guard stood down passed 3247 with only the guard's own 2 tests failing (expected).
  The failing set changes run-to-run, confirming non-determinism.

## Suggested improvements
- Make the nested-runner tests resilient to test-semaphore saturation (raise/derive
  their subprocess timeout, or inject a test-only slot/`TEST_LOCK_TIMEOUT`).
- Consider excluding `refs/remotes/origin/*` (and other-actor branch churn) from the
  live-repo guard fingerprint, or only arming it for refs the suite can create.

## Acceptance criteria
- AC1: Nested `run_tests.py` tests do not time out purely because the host test
  semaphore is busy.
- AC2: The live-repo guard does not fail a run when only external `origin/*` refs move.
- AC3: Full suite is green on a shared host with ≥3 concurrent agent test runs.
